book01.title: 1,000 Places to See Before You Die
book01.author: Patricia Schultz
book01.description: This original bucket list contains a wide variety of stunning places around the globe! A must-have in every globetrotter's library, even if it's purely aspirational.

book02.author: Stephen King
book02.description: A time-traveling splendour from the King. What would you do if you had the opportunity to change history for the better? A chilling political journey into the United States' past, with King's usual wit.

book03.title: 1st to Die
book03.author: James Patterson
book03.description: This thrilling first book in the Women's Murder Club series takes four crime-solving friends through a classic murder mystery. Will they make it through the twists this case has in store for them?

book04.title: The 7 Stages of Grieving
book04.author: Wesley Enoch & Deborah Mailman
book04.description: A powerful one-woman play about an Aboriginal woman delivering a series of direct-address monologues and poems connecting the recent death of her Nana with the larger cycles of oppression and grief caused by Australia's colonial history and racist present.

book05.title: 84, Charing Cross Road
book05.author: Helene Hanff
book05.description: An epistolary memoir about a friendship that develops over a shared love of books. A lighthearted, humorous collection of letters between a bookseller in London and a writer in New York City, desperate to fill gaps in her collection.

book06.title: A Dance With Dragons
book06.author: George R. R. Martin
book06.description: Who would have thought that the fifth tome in the ASOIAF series has even more dragons, complex politics, and mysterious betrayals in store for us than ever before? Also, George, if you read this: Winds of Winter when?!

book07.title: A Deepness in the Sky
book07.author: Vernor Vinge
book07.description: An interstellar trade conflict unfolds between two rivalling powers in this epic and thought-provoking sci-fi prequel. A dramatic modern classic of speculative sci-fi!

book08.title: Design Patterns; Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
book08.author: E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson, J. Vlissides
book08.description: The classic reference for object-oriented programming, written by the legendary Gang of Four: a catalogue of reusable solutions to that solve common problems and make your code cleaner, reusable, and future-proof

book09.title: A Dictionary of the English Language
book09.author: Samuel Johnson
book09.description: I've heard the 1740s were a good decade for the English language. Check out lots of words and their meanings in this slightly outdated collection.

book10.title: A Fire Upon the Deep
book10.author: Vernor Vinge
book10.description: Buckle up for an epic space adventure that kicks off the Zones of Thought series and introduces a mind-bending future thousands of years from now.

book11.title: A Fire Upon the Deep
book11.author: James Lovegrove & Nancy Holder
book11.description: This book series continues the story of the Serenity's Crew we never got to see in the TV series. Bounty hunters, hired criminals, mysterious research labs, brown coats, homey spaceships, allies, enemies, laughter, and drama... This space western has it all!

book12.title: A Game of Thrones
book12.author: George R. R. Martin
book12.description: Stern lords, ambitious ladies, rising queens, and underestimated bastards. This book kicks off an epic fantasy saga full of tragedy, twists, and undead. Winter is coming, and so is the drama!

book13.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
book13.author: Holly Jackson
book13.description: Everyone in her small town believes the case to be solved. But when young Pippa starts digging up the details of a murder from years past for her final school project, she discovers secrets yet untold.

book14.title: A Room of One's Own
book14.author: Virginia Woolf
book14.description: This classic piece by Virginia Woolf is both a thought-provoking essay and a narrative exploration of the position of women as characters, as well as writers, in a literary tradition dominated by the patriarchy.

book15.title: Rosalind Franklin; The Dark Lady of DNA
book15.author: Brenda Maddox
book15.description: Rosalind Franklin's contribution to one of the greatest discoveries of the 20th century wasn't acknowledged during her lifetime. This is an excellent biography of the woman whose research was crucial in determining the structure of DNA.

book16.title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
book16.author: Bill Bryson
book16.description: From atoms to galaxies, this popular science book takes readers on a wild journey through the past, uncovering the secrets of our fascinating universe. For all of those readers out there who are interested in nearly everything.

book17.title: A Storm of Swords
book17.author: George R. R. Martin
book17.description: War still wages in the Seven Kingdoms, the lands of the ASOIAF fantasy series. Alliances are made just as quickly as they are broken. And don't even get me started on the weddings.

book18.title: A Study in Scarlet
book18.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
book18.description: In this first appearance of the eccentric detective Sherlock Holmes and his partner Dr Watson, the pair take out the old magnifying glass to solve a murder case in Victorian London.

book19.title: A Time to Kill
book19.author: John Grisham
book19.description: In this tragic legal drama by John Grisham, set in a fictional county of 1980s Mississippi, the young attorney Jake Brigance attempts to let justice prevail even in a world full of racial injustice.

book20.title: A Wrinkle in Time
book20.author: Madeleine L'Engle
book20.description: This "science fantasy" adventure starts off the classic Time Quintet series where three young heroes travel through time and space and face matters of good and evil.

book21.title: ABCC; A Bookstonbury Crochet Collection
book21.author: Various Authors
book21.description: Crochet your favourite Bookstonian icons and create your own pocket-sized version of our beautiful town! 120 easy-to-follow and cosy patterns, such as: St Bookston, Raw Fish, Seagull, Mobile Bookshop, Dog, Plants, and many more!

book22.title: Abridgment of Murray's English Grammar
book22.author: Lindley Murray
book22.description: Grammar is entirely made up! It can't hurt you! But, since most of us have to practise it anyway, why not make it fun with this early nineteenth-century American school guide?

book23.title: Ace; What Asexuality Reveals About Desire, Society and the Meaning of Sex
book23.author: Angela Chen
book23.description: What does it mean to be asexual? Reimagine human connection by exploring intersections of identity, sexuality and culture through a collection of critiques, reflections and conversations with community.

book24.title: The Acts of King Arthur and His Noble Knights
book24.author: John Steinbeck
book24.description: This adaptation of Malory's Morte d'Arthur (The Death of King Arthur) was published after the author's death. Steinbeck tried using modern language within the frame of Middle English. Proving yet again that authors with weird fixations write the most interesting books.

book25.title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn; Adventures of Tom and Huck #2
book25.author: Mark Twain
book25.description: Mark Twain shows us the hypocrisy of 19th century Mississippi through the dawning understanding of a young boy's conscience. From the evils of slavery to toxic masculinity, Huck has to reckon with what he sees and decide for himself. And it takes him a while...

book26.title: After the Funeral
book26.author: Agatha Christie
book26.description: Usually, death precedes a funeral. But with this English family, things go awry quickly, and only Detective Poirot can help them find out who dun did it now.

book27.title: Alanna; The First Adventure (The Song of the Lioness #1)
book27.author: Tamora Pierce
book27.description: Alanna disguises herself as a boy to become a knight - but keeping that secret in between combat training, dealing with her magical Gift, making friends (and enemies!), and growing up is a tall order in this foundational youth fantasy work.

book28.title: Alias Grace
book28.author: Margaret Atwood
book28.description: In this narrativised version of a historical murder case, a young woman's crimes come into question when she is released from prison. Is Grace Marks really a killer?

book29.title: Alvar Aalto
book29.author: Alvar Aalto
book29.description: Get to know the Finnish design master Alvar Aalto, as this book takes us on a visual journey through almost sixty years of iconic creations, including photographs, plans, and sketches.

book30.title: Amadeus
book30.author: Peter Shaffer
book30.description: Salieri's dreams of becoming history's best composer are threatened when childish upstart Mozart wows Vienna with his musical genius. Can Salieri ruin Mozart's career in time? A play about ambition, treachery, and the lengths one will go for fame.

book31.title: American Psycho
book31.author: Bret Easton Ellis
book31.description: American Psycho details the increasingly dark and violent stream-of-consciousness of a young, rich, narcissistic yuppie working on Wall Street in 90s Manhattan. Contains graphic descriptions of gore and violence.

book32.title: Among the Hidden; (The Shadow Children #1)
book32.author: Margaret Peterson Haddix
book32.description: As the third child in his family, Luke's very existence is forbidden. When he meets another forbidden child, can the pair execute a dangerous plan to escape the shadows? The first in the dystopian Shadow Children series.

book33.title: Anathem
book33.author: Neal Stephenson
book33.description: What happens when all of the planet's intellectuals are shut off from the rest of the world, left to ponder existence without ever experiencing it? Find out in this epic and ambitious sci-fi page-turner.

book34.title: Ancillary Justice; Imperial Radch #1
book34.author: Ann Leckie
book34.description: What would you do if you were a giant spaceship controlling hundreds of soldiers, now betrayed and trapped in one fragile body? If you're like Breq, you'd take revenge on the colonial empire that made you?

book35.title: And The World Spins Anyway
book35.author: Georgie Jones
book35.description: In the author's debut collection of poetry and short stories, she invites readers to take a step away from social media and feel a little less alone in this chaotic, beautiful world. A refreshing and relatable read.

book36.title: Angels & Demons
book36.author: Dan Brown
book36.description: The first in a series of thrilling mystery novels, Angels & Demons entails an elaborate assassination plot on high-ranking Vatican officials. But what did the mysterious Illuminati have to do with it all?

book37.title: Angels in America; A Gay Fantasia on National Themes
book37.author: Tony Kushner
book37.description: A play so long it's traditionally shown over two consecutive days, Angels in America explores the 1980's American AIDS crisis in a surrealist deconstruction of religion and sexual identity.

book38.title: Animal Farm
book38.author: George Orwell
book38.description: The allegorical tale of anthropomorphic farm animals, who overthrow the farmer's rule over them and attempt to lead the farm themselves. It is one of the most important pieces of 20th-century political satire, asking: What happens after the revolution?

book39.title: The Animals of Farthing Wood
book39.author: Colin Dann
book39.description: The book behind a TV series that traumatized an entire generation recounts the journey of Fox, Badger, Mole and the other inhabitants of Farthing Wood as they strike out trying to find a new home. Their heart-breaking story continues in a further six books.

book40.title: Annabel Lee
book40.author: Edgar Allen Poe
book40.description: Poe's verses shines beautifully in this haunting and tragic tale of forbidden love. Annabel Lee us a classic poem which immerses the reader in an eerie atmosphere and makes them long for a ghostly girl.

book41.title: Architecture in Britain; 1530-1830
book41.author: John N. Summerson
book41.description: From the Renaissance to Neoclassicism, this guide charts the development of English architectural theory and practice, alongside marvellous colour photographs by A.F. Kersting.

book42.title: Ariel
book42.author: Sylvia Plath
book42.description: A collection of poems, some tender, some despairing, some nihilistic, and so much more. Written in the last three years before Plath's death and published posthumously.

book43.title: Arnheim's Principles of Athletic Training; A Competency-Based Approach
book43.author: William E. Prentice
book43.description: This book is so competency-based, you'll be diagnosing old injuries in everyone you see and testing range of motion on yourself constantly. Learn how to treat sprained ankles, wrap a bandage, and other helpful training tips for the average athlete. Possibly outdated!

book44.title: Around the World in Eighty Days
book44.author: Jules Verne
book44.description: When an eccentric Englishman's unwavering punctuality is questioned, he wagers that he can circumnavigate the world in only 80 days, and we follow his almost impossible journey.

book45.title: Art of the Modern Movie Poster; International Postwar Style and Design
book45.author: Various Authors
book45.description: A lovely collection of over 1,500 vintage film posters, perfect for any film buff, poster-collector, or owner of a coffee table.

book46.title: Artemis Fowl
book46.author: Eoin Colfer
book46.description: When criminally inclined teenager Artemis tries to restore his family's fortune, he accidentally messes with the wrong fairies. Suddenly, he finds himself amidst a folk of high-tech fae.

book47.title: As Good As Dead
book47.author: Holly Jackson
book47.description: The finale to the Good Girl's Guide to Murder YA series and a catching mystery for any true crime podcast fans out there. Will our titular Good Girl make it out unscathed?

book48.title: Ashfall Legacy; Ashfall #1
book48.author: Pittacus Lore
book48.description: Syd Chambers, alien-human hybrid, has never known his father, a Denza native who disappeared years ago. Picking up the trail, Syd now journeys beyond Earth to seek out his father, discovering a universe-shattering secret along the way.

book49.title: Assassin's Apprentice; The Farseer Trilogy Book One
book49.author: Robin Hobb
book49.description: Fitz was born out of wedlock to the crown prince, and for that, he is hated. Join Fitz as he learns the politics and intrigue of the palace whilst being raised in the stables. Does he have a touch of the Farseer magic that is so vied for by the royal family?

book50.title: Asterios Polyp
book50.author: David Mazzucchelli
book50.description: Asterios is one of the world's greatest architects. This award-winning graphic novel follows how the rigid lines of his personality and architectural style shatter, sending him on an aimless journey that transforms a once self-absorbed man into someone who cares.

book51.title: At the Earth's Core
book51.author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
book51.description: The Hollow Earth sci-fi novel for anyone who read 1864's Journey to the Centre of the Earth and thought: "Not enough dinosaurs!"

book52.title: Atmosphere
book52.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
book52.description: Joan Goodwin has always loved the stars. When she’s selected for NASA’s new astronaut programme, she finds friendship, purpose, and a love she never expected. But one mission will change everything.

book53.title: Attack On Titan; Volume 1
book53.author: Hajime Isayama
book53.description: Eren Yeager has sworn to take revenge on the giant humanoid creatures known as Titans, who destroyed his home and killed his mother. An action-packed and thrilling first volume of the dystopian fantasy manga.

book54.title: Babel; or the Necessity of Violence
book54.author: R. F. Kuang
book54.description: This novel explores an alternate-reality British Empire, in which languages and their meanings are harnessed for their immense magical power.

book55.title: Beloved
book55.author: Toni Morrison
book55.description: An unrivalled piece of gothic historical fiction by Toni Morrison, a master of magical realism. Beloved tells a story about the trauma of slavery and how past hurt can linger like a ghost.

book56.title: Better Than the Movies
book56.author: Lynn Painter
book56.description: Liz is on a quest for a teen love story like in the movies. Can her annoying neighbour Wes really help her go to prom with her crush? And why does he have to be so attractive?

book57.title: Call Me by Your Name
book57.author: André Aciman
book57.description: Their big age gap seems to be unable to deter Elio and Oliver from their obsession with each other, and they experience the highs and lows of a gay summer romance in 1980s Italy.

book58.title: Camp Damascus
book58.author: Chuck Tingle
book58.description: Rose has started receiving demonic visions and coughing up swarms of flies. Her investigations into why keep leading her to the gay conversion camp run by her Christian community. But she's never been there before—or has she?

book59.title: Can't Spell Treason Without Tea; Tomes and Tea #1
book59.author: Rebecca Thorne
book59.description: Come along with Reyna and Kianthe as they escape the clutches of cruel queens and mage obligations in order to open their dream bookshop and tea salon. Watch as the two women fall even more in love and slowly find their place in the world. And what's this about dragons?

book60.title: Cat's Eye
book60.author: Margaret Atwood
book60.description: Cat's Eye tells the tale of a woman's art, memory, and a childhood friendship gone awry. How can she come to terms with her past?

book61.title: Catcher in the Rye, The
book61.author: JD Salinger
book61.description: Holden Caulfield thinks you're a phony. A disaffected teenager travels around 1950's New York City after he's expelled from school. A literary classic with pages of casually-written monologues lamenting alienation, depression, and the inauthenticity of adults.

book62.title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
book62.author: Roald Dahl
book62.description: Only five lucky winners of a golden ticket will be allowed to discover the true goings-on in Willy Wonka's magical chocolate factory. Join them in this illustrated children's tale.

book63.title: Charlotte's Web
book63.author: E. B. White
book63.description: When a clever spider and a radiant pig become friends, what could stand in their way? A charming children's classic with beautiful illustrations.

book64.title: Chemical Chaos; Horrible Science
book64.author: Nick Arnold & Tony De Saulles
book64.description: Chemistry is confusing, and chemistry lessons are boring. Fret not! For this book is not about the bits you learn in school—but the funny bits, the fascinating bits and the bits that end up in blasts and bangs and dodgy discoveries!

book65.title: Charmed Life; (Chrestomanci, Book 1)
book65.author: Diana Wynne Jones
book65.description: In the first of the Chrestomanci Series we meet Eric 'Cat' Chant. After the death of his parents, he and his sister move into Chrestomanci Castle to live with the world's most powerful enchanter and his family. Things, however, aren't quote what they appear to be.

book66.title: Chemistry; The Central Science
book66.author: Theodore L. Brown
book66.description: An essential guide for all students looking to expand their knowledge of the sciences. This classic textbook contains all the essentials to begin understanding the squishiest of all sciences.

book67.title: The Chicago Manual of Style (CMOS)
book67.author: University of Chicago Press
book67.description: Are you playing pin-the-hyphen with your sentences? Currently lost in a forest of commas? Worry no more, with 200+ pages of writing rules for publications, in this vintage style guide used by academics and (some) trade publishers!

book68.title: A Child's Garden of Verses
book68.author: Robert Louis Stevenson & Tasha Tudor
book68.description: A collection of sixty-six poems for imaginative children, accompanied by the gentle watercolour illustrations of Tasha Tudor.

book69.title: Children of Time; (Book 1)
book69.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
book69.description: An experiment into accelerated evolution on a terraformed planet was thwarted, but evolution still finds a way. Even on a planet lightyears away, this series presents our society with a mirror when it shows us the problems of a different species. Arachnophobes beware!

book70.title: Chocolat; Book 1
book70.author: Joanne Harris
book70.description: Vianne's new chocolaterie is a refuge for the over-looked townspeople of Lansquenet. Customers are given a mug of bittersweet hot chocolate, a sympathetic ear, and just a touch of magic-much to the disapproval of the local priest.

book71.title: Circe
book71.author: Madeline Miller
book71.description: You might know her story already, as Odysseus tells it. But in this modern retelling of Greek mythology, the tale of the sorceress on her island gains a whole new depth.

book72.title: Clap When You Land
book72.author: Elizabeth Acevedo
book72.description: Yahaira has lost her father, her hero. Camino has lost her father, a near stranger. Both have gained a sister. In this powerful story written in verse, two girls learn to grieve and dream together.

book73.title: Cleopatra and Frankenstein
book73.author: Coco Mellors
book73.description: A whirlwind marriage between a young painter and a wealthy older man reshapes the lives of everyone around them. Funny, messy, and moving, this novel explores love, identity, friendship, and the strange ways we grow up.

book74.title: Collected Poems; 1934-1952
book74.author: Dylan Thomas
book74.description: One of the most important Welsh poets of the 20th century, Thomas' writing is lauded for its strong imagery and thought-provoking depths. Recommended reading for the seaside!

book75.title: Confess
book75.author: Colleen Hoover
book75.description: As Auburn is trying to rebuild her life, she is instantly smitten with the mysterious artist Owen. But can their relationship last as his past is revealed? A suspenseful adult romance unfolds.

book76.title: Conversations with Friends
book76.author: Sally Rooney
book76.description: This novel follows Frances as she navigates the complex relationships with her best friend and ex-girlfriend, Bobbi, and an older married couple, Nick and Melissa. A piercing exploration of blurred boundaries of intimacy and the struggles of one's identity.

book77.title: Dark Age; (Red Rising #5)
book77.author: Pierce Brown
book77.description: The war for the solar system continues. When peace has a different meaning to everyone, what does it mean to be a hero? This violent space opera is packed with political intrigue. Whose army will prove itself victorious? And what does victory look like in this truly Dark Age?

book78.title: The Dark is Rising
book78.author: Susan Cooper
book78.description: Following a terrifying night, Will wakes on his 11th birthday to a world covered in snow and a world changed. Will learns that he is one of the Old Ones and joins the battle against the Dark. Second in a classic fantasy series for kids.

book79.title: Dark Matter
book79.author: Blake Crouch
book79.description: A thrilling action plot unfolds when ordinary physics professor Jason is abducted and finds himself in a parallel world. What dark paths will he face to make it back to his old life?

book80.title: Dark Places
book80.author: Gillian Flynn
book80.description: Little Libby's life in rural Kansas is forever changed when she witnesses the murder of her family. Twenty-four years later, she revisits it all for the entertainment of crime-loving strangers.

book81.title: The Dark Portal; Book One of The Deptford Mice
book81.author: Robin Jarvis
book81.description: No one has ever seen Jupiter, the living god worshipped by rats living below Deptford. In this dark fantasy, Audrey, a young mouse, ventures into the sewers where she discovers her missing father was last seen in Jupiter's altar chamber. A thrilling read for kids.

book82.title: Death in Yellowstone; Accidents and Foolhardiness in the First National Park
book82.author: Lee H. Whittlesey
book82.description: Grizzly bear attacks, hot springs, and avalanches, oh my ! Cautionary tales about what not to do in one of America's wildest national parks.

book83.title: Death Note; Volume 1
book83.author: Tsugumi Ohba
book83.description: When the power over life and death falls into the hands of Light Yagami, the young student vows to use it for good. But death god Ryuk might have other plans.

book84.title: Death of a Salesman; Certain Private Conversations in Two Acts and a Requiem
book84.author: Arthur Miller
book84.description: It's 1940 and Willy Loman is as fatally insecure as his career. This depressing play asks whether the pursuit of the consumerist American dream is really all it's cracked up to be.

book85.title: Death on the Nile
book85.author: Agatha Christie
book85.description: Detective Poirot is keeping to the background on his Egyptian vacation to carefully observe the mystery unfolding before him. Everyone had a motive, but who is cold-blooded enough to be the killer?

book86.title: Divergent
book86.author: Veronica Roth
book86.description: In a post-apocalyptic Chicago, sixteen-year-old Tris is left with no choice but to join one of five factions. Prepare for an action-packed, dystopian story for young adult readers.

book87.title: Down Under
book87.author: Bill Bryson
book87.description: An entertaining yet educational travelogue exploring a Sunburned Country , also known as Australia. Marvel about the country's people, history, landscape, flora and fauna.

book88.title: Dracula
book88.author: Bram Stoker
book88.description: A chilling classic that masterfully mixes the 19th-century epistolary novel with early gothic horror. It follows boring businessman Jonathan Harker on a trip to a certain Transylvanian castle...

book89.title: Dragonsong
book89.author: Anne McCaffrey
book89.description: Menolly can't stay in her fishing village, which forbids her dreams and confines her to rigid gender roles. Surprisingly, the new life awaiting her holds songs and dragons in store.

book90.title: Dreamer's Pool; Blackthorn & Grim #1
book90.author: Juliet Marillier
book90.description: Two new friends start new lives after a magical escape. Blackthorn is a healer, Grim does physical labor. The duo's work on a local crime draws the Prince's attention. He needs their help with a problem of his own. A fantasy trilogy with slow-burn romance!

book91.title: The Dry; (Aaron Falk #1)
book91.author: Jane Harper
book91.description: Police investigator Aaron Falk returns home for the funeral of his friend in the small Australian town that shunned him years ago. In this outback mystery, Falk uncovers not just how his friend died, but how it's connected to the crime he was framed for years ago.

book92.title: Emma
book92.author: Jane Austen
book92.description: In this comedy of manners from Austen, socialite Emma is very confident in her matchmaking skills. But when will she learn that not everyone appreciates her meddling?

book93.title: Empire of the Vampire
book93.author: Jay Kristoff
book93.description: With the sun vanished and vampires ascendant, Gabriel de León is humanity's last silversaint and their last hope. Imprisoned by his enemies, he recounts battles, heartbreak, and the perilous chase for the Holy Grail.

book94.title: Fantastic Mr Fox
book94.author: Roald Dahl
book94.description: A clever fox and his family set out to outsmart their farming neighbours in this charmingly illustrated classic children's novel.

book95.title: Far from the Madding Crowd
book95.author: Thomas Hardy
book95.description: Bathsheba Everdene thinks she's all that. Three men are reluctant to contradict her and eager to win her affections. A foggy, moody novel in a provincial setting with tragic plot twists and beautiful nature writing.

book96.title: Feminist, Queer, Crip
book96.author: Alison Kafer
book96.description: In this work, Professor Alison Kafer proposes a critical framework that imagines another future for disabled and queer bodies and rejects the idea of disability as a predetermined limit.

book97.title: Femme in Public
book97.author: Alok V Menom
book97.description: Queer artist Alok shares their journey navigating family and American society as a gender non-conforming, Indian diasporic, transfemme in this heartfelt collection of poems.

book98.title: Ficciones
book98.author: J. L. Borges, A. Bonner & A. Kerrigan
book98.description: 17 masterful short stories from the Argentinian writer and poet, famous for his maze-like prose. Fantastical, intellectual, and bizarre. This selection includes The Library of Babel , The Circular Ruins , and The God of the Labyrinth .

book99.title: The Field Guide; The Spiderwick Chronicles #1
book99.author: Holly Black & Tony DiTerlizzi
book99.description: When Jared, Simon, and Mallory dust off a field guide to the hidden world of faerie, the siblings learn the dangerous, fantastical creatures are a little too close to their new home. Book one of a magical children's series.

book100.title: Five Little Peppers and How They Grew; Five Little Peppers #1
book100.author: Margaret Sidney Porter
book100.description: A cosy classic about five children and their mother, living in a little brown house, learning to be helpful and create their own happiness in lean times. Who knew baked goods and surprise visits could bring so much joy?

book101.title: Five on a Treasure Island
book101.author: Enid Blyton
book101.description: A childhood adventure with five friends, a shipwreck, and a hidden treasure. The first in the classic Famous Five series of children's mystery novels.

book102.title: Five Survive
book102.author: Holly Jackson
book102.description: Red and her five friends are headed for Spring Break at the beach. But when their RV breaks down, the young adults are stranded. A killer plans to silence one of their group. Can they find out who they want before the night takes them all?

book103.title: A Florence Diary
book103.author: Diana Athill
book103.description: A charming diary, chronicling Athill's fortnight in Italy, 1947. Illustrated with delightful black and white photos of Florence, this little book captures an era of travel that has been lost to time.

book104.title: Flower Fables
book104.author: Louisa May Alcott
book104.description: A collection of fairy stories and poems, Flower Fables is a charming and delightful book, illustrated and easy to read for children and adults of any age.

book105.title: Flowers for Algernon
book105.author: Daniel Keyes
book105.description: A science-fiction short story turned novel, which grapples with the meaning of intelligence, disability, and the consequences of human augmentation in the name of progress.

book106.title: The Forests of Silence; (Deltora Quest #1)
book106.author: Emily Rodda
book106.description: In this epic quest for young readers, a pair of unexpected heroes must face untold dangers as they search for the long magical gems that could save them from the tyrannical Shadow Lowd. Their first destination? The Forests of Silence.

book107.title: The Forgotten Beasts of Eld
book107.author: Patricia A. McKillip
book107.description: Sybel's closest friends are magical animals. She's more than content to avoid the war brewing in neighboring kingdoms. But when a soldier brings a human baby into her fantastical menagerie for safekeeping, her safe little world will never be the same.

book108.title: Frog and Toad Together
book108.author: Arnold Lobel
book108.description: Oh, to garden, bike, and go on adventures with your soulmate! While these short stories might strictly qualify as children's literature, who doesn't yearn for the life of Frog and Toad?

book109.title: Full Dark, No Stars
book109.author: Stephen King
book109.description: Four chilling and devastating novellas by Stephen King, dealing with the darkness of retribution and revenge. True horror, read with care!

book110.title: Games, Game Design, Game Studies
book110.author: Gundolf S. Freyermuth
book110.description: The must-read primer for anyone seeking to become a serious games scholar.

book111.title: The Garden of Evening Mists
book111.author: Tan Twan Eng
book111.description: Set in post-war Malaya, this story follows Yun Ling, a war-crime survivor and retired judge, through a shifting timeline between 1980s and flashbacks to 1949, as she seeks solace in the lush highlands of her childhood.

book112.title: Gone Girl
book112.author: Gillian Flynn
book112.description: Following the blossoming relationship of Nick and Amy, we flash forward to their fifth wedding anniversary, where Amy has suddenly disappeared... Has Nick become a man capable of killing his wife?

book113.title: Good Girl, Bad Blood
book113.author: Holly Jackson
book113.description: Student investigator turned podcaster Pippa is trying to leave her detective days behind. But how can she ignore this recent disappearance, when the police won't even investigate?

book114.title: Good Night, Gorilla
book114.author: Peggy Rathmann
book114.description: When the zookeeper isn't looking, this little gorilla isn't the only animal who sneaks out of the zoo. A short and sweet bedtime story for the little ones.

book116.title: A Gothic Cookbook; Hauntingly Delicious Recipes Inspired by 13 Classic Tales
book116.author: Ella Buchan & Dr Allesandra Pino
book116.description: Feast your way through thirteen Gothic stories, from The Bloody Chamber to The Woman in White. The illustrated cookbook that invites readers to devour the literary classics.

book117.title: Gregor the Overlander
book117.author: Suzanne Collins
book117.description: Gregor discovers a hidden world beneath New York City in this charming, yet dangerous fantasy adventure for young readers. Will he live up to the prophecy foretelling his deeds?

book118.title: Gulliver's Travels
book118.author: Jonathan Swift
book118.description: Through the various travels of Gulliver, this proto-science fiction novel satirises the political environment of England and the travelogues popular during its colonial expansions.

book119.title: Hamlet
book119.author: William Shakespeare
book119.description: This Danish prince suddenly has a lot going on. His father is dead, his uncle is evil, and his mother is quickly getting remarried... So, it is entirely understandable that Hamlet now plunges into a crisis.

book120.title: Hamnet
book120.author: Maggie O'Farrell
book120.description: Stratford-upon-Avon, 1596 - A marriage is on the rocks, and a sudden illness threatens the life of a child. A short, tragic, and intricate novel about the familial inspiration behind one of the world's most famous plays. It never mentions the playwright by name!

book121.title: Heartstopper; Volume 1
book121.author: Alice Oseman
book121.description: The heartwarming graphic novel where Nick and Charlie meet at a grammar school for boys. Prepare to giggle and blush while watching sparks unfold between them!

book122.title: Heidi
book122.author: Johanna Spyri
book122.description: The heartwarming story of little Heidi, who lives with her grandfather in the Swiss Alps, changing the lives of those around her for the better. A classic for children all around the world.

book123.title: The Hobbit; The Lord of the Rings #0
book123.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
book123.description: You never know what'll happen when you step outside your front door. Especially if a wizard left his mark on said door. Bilbo leaves his creature comforts behind to seek adventure with a company of dwarves, and winds up bringing home the worst souvenir possible.

book124.title: Homage to Catalonia
book124.author: George Orwell
book124.description: An exceptionally observant, vivid, and often witty journalistic work turned memoir by George Orwell, wherein he tells of his time fighting fascists in the Spanish Civil War.

book125.title: Home Before Dark
book125.author: Riley Sager
book125.description: Her father's last words were: "Stay away from the house, it's not safe for you." Maggie gives her word. But later, she discovers she's inherited the spooky house that made her father famous. Can't hurt to visit... right? A horror/thriller with a book-within-a-book format.

book126.title: Howl's Moving Castle
book126.author: Diana Wynne Jones
book126.description: Sophie seeks out the mysterious wizard Howl, and his ever-moving castle, since he might be her only chance of breaking her enchantment. Is there more to his heartlessness than meets the eye?

book127.title: If Not, Winter; (Fragments of Sappho)
book127.author: Sappho, transl. by A. Carson
book127.description: A collection of ancient fragments, this book offers a glimpse into the captivating poetry of a mysterious Greek writer whose verses of passion (for women) have stood the test of time.

book128.title: If We Were Villains
book128.author: M. L. Rio
book128.description: Seven acting students at an elite arts college are very familiar with Shakespearean drama. But soon, the fictional power struggles and love entanglements they enact become their reality, too.

book129.title: The Illustrated Dust Jacket, 1920-1970
book129.author: Martin Salisbury
book129.description: In this collection of cover art, you'll see the historical evolution of style and intention in book jacket design: From practical tool to key marketing element. Go ahead and judge books by their cover!

book130.title: In Cold Blood
book130.author: Truman Capote
book130.description: Murder, mystery, and chilling psychology intertwine in this pioneering work in the true crime genre, as Capote (and his friend Harper Lee) extensively research a 1959 case.

book131.title: Inferno
book131.author: Dante Alighieri, transl. by A. Esolen
book131.description: The first part of the epic Divine Comedy , and the most famous work of self-insert bible fanfiction to date. Wherein Dante and Virgil delve deep through the nine circles of hell.

book132.title: The Inheritance Games
book132.author: Jennifer Lynn Barnes
book132.description: This thrilling mystery for young adults kicks off a series of novels surrounding Avery, a teenager who suddenly becomes heir to a strange billionaire's fortune. If she can make it that far...

book133.title: It
book133.author: Stephen King
book133.description: This one will certainly make you afraid of clowns, balloons and storm drains... if you aren't already. A staple of small-town horror fiction, It makes children's nightmares a reality.

book134.title: Italian Villas and Their Gardens
book134.author: Edith Wharton
book134.description: Sixteen years before her famous novel, The Age of Innocence , Wharton publishes this scholarly travel book. It is a remarkably detailed survey of Italian garden architecture.

book135.title: James and the Giant Peach
book135.author: Roald Dahl
book135.description: This fantastical adventure follows James into a peachy realm populated by friendly worms and bugs. An illustrated book perfect for children.

book136.title: Journey to the Centre of the Earth
book136.author: Jules Verne
book136.description: Have you always wanted to meet a dinosaur? Easy, just hop down an Icelandic volcano and check at the Earth's core. They should hopefully still be there.

book137.title: Julie Chan is Dead
book137.author: Liann Zhang
book137.description: When Julie finds her influencer twin dead, she slips into her glamorous life. Designer wardrobe, perfect skin, millions of followers. But on an exclusice island retreat, she learns Chloe's world was far from flawless. And someone wants the new "Chloe" gone too.

book138.title: Julius Caesar
book138.author: William Shakespeare
book138.description: Who's up for a political assassination with the homies? Come on. It's for the good of Rome, right? — No! Wrong! Et tu, Brute?!

book139.title: Jurassic Park
book139.author: Michael Crichton
book139.description: IT'S JURASSIC PARK, IT'S A MASSIVE PARK! Filled with more dinosaurs and danger than you can shake a stick at. A slightly misguided scientist decided to give dinosaurs another chance, and thinks it would be great if the public could come and have a nose at them too.

book140.title: Kiki's Delivery Service
book140.author: Eiko Kadono
book140.description: A spirited young witch needs to learn how to stand on her own two feet as she arrives in a bustling and charming seaside town. Sound familiar, anyone?

book141.title: King Stakh's Wild Hunt
book141.author: Uladzimir Karatkievich
book141.description: Something stalks the foggy marsh as a young folklorist finds himself lost in a family's cursed manor. Will he be able to figure out or fall to the Wild Hunt ? Mysterious and gothic, this Belarusian classic continues to haunt.

book142.title: Henry V
book142.author: William Shakespeare
book142.description: Shakespeare's next Henry must prove his might in a war against France in this dramatic retelling of English history. And he's certainly nailing the speeches!

book143.title: Labyrinths
book143.author: Jorge Luis Borges
book143.description: Labyrinths: Selected Stories & Other Writings is a representative selection of essays, short stories, and parables written by Argentine poet Borges and translated into English.

book144.title: Lady Audley's Secret
book144.author: Mary Elizabeth Braddon
book144.description: A scandalous domestic thriller complete with a twisty murder mystery, and a layered anti-heroine. Surprisingly feminist for the Victorian era!

book145.title: Le Corbusier
book145.author: Le Corbusier
book145.description: Known as a designer of brutalist buildings, this collection of his projects illustrates Le Corbusier's belief in better living conditions for the increasingly crowded cities of the 20th century.

book146.title: Leave Taking
book146.author: Winsome Pinnock
book146.description: A humorous play about a British-Caribbean mother and her two daughters transposing their Jamaican heritage in 1980's London. Leave Taking was the first play by a black female playwright to premiere at the Royal National Theatre in 1987.

book147.title: Little Women
book147.author: Louisa May Alcott
book147.description: The four March sisters navigate love, loss, and the trials of growing up into womanhood, as their coming-of-age story reflects parts of Alcott's own youth.

book148.title: Love
book148.author: Toni Morrison
book148.description: A contemporary classic by Morrison, which follows three generations of Black women, the aftermath of a man's death, and their complicated relationships to him and each other.

book149.title: Macbeth
book149.author: William Shakespeare
book149.description: One couple of Scottish aristocrats start to believe that they deserve a bigger piece of the cake. And they decide to make it everyone else's problem...

book150.title: Mend! A Refashioning Manual and Manifesto
book150.author: Kate Sekules
book150.description: Decrease the number of clothes you toss, and learn how to repair them in ways that make them a work of art! A how-to guide explaining the process and possibilities of mending, perfect for the experienced sewist or the person who's never picked up a needle.

book151.title: Meridian
book151.author: Alice Walker
book151.description: The captivating story of Meridian Hill, a female activist in the Civil Rights Movement of the 1960s and 70s, and her political and personal revolutions in life.

book152.title: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood
book152.author: Howard Pyle
book152.description: Follow the adventures of the merry bandit who robbed from the rich to give to the poor. Pyle, an American illustrator, wrote this version of the legend especially for children, and this edition features his humorous illustrations.

book153.title: Merry Mister Meddle; Mister Meddle Series
book153.author: Enid Blyton
book153.description: A collection of humorous tales about Mister Meddle and his disastrous attempts at being helpful; like putting a 'growing-spell; in a wash-tub to help with laundry or mistaking glue for treacle that he uses to spruce up his aunt's pudding!

book154.title: Middlemarch
book154.author: George Eliot
book154.description: A charming study of English provincial life, with all of its love, ambition, and scandal. Follow the lives of unforgettable characters in this literary classic.

book155.title: milk and honey
book155.author: Rupi Kaur
book155.description: A poetic journey through heartbreak and healing and the hurt and love that come with 21st-century womanhood.

book156.title: Misery
book156.author: Stephen King
book156.description: An obsessive fan has no plans of ever letting her favourite romance author go... Another cocaine-fueled 80s horror classic.

book157.title: Moby-Dick
book157.author: Herman Melville
book157.description: A maniacal pursuit, an enigmatic white giant, and a captain obsessed with vengeance. A commercial failure, and "the greatest book of the sea ever written", according to Walter.

book158.title: Momo; or, The Grey Gentlemen
book158.author: Michael Ende
book158.description: A strange story of time thieves and a curious child on a mission to return stolen time and joy to her town. Get inspired by this children's classic!

book159.title: Journey to the West; or, Monkey King
book159.author: Wu Cheng'en
book159.description: A mischievous shapeshifter embarks on a legendary adventure, based on folk tales and legends, in this timeless Chinese classic.

book160.title: The Journey; Big Panda and Tiny Dragon #2
book160.author: James Norbury
book160.description: The adventures of Big Panda and Tiny Dragon continue as they navigate some of life's trying moments. Accompanied by charming illustrations, this is a beautiful picture book about friendship and overcoming adversity.

book161.title: Murder on the Orient Express
book161.author: Agatha Christie
book161.description: What better place to murder someone than on the world-famous Orient Express? Only the killer forgot that the genius detective Hercule Poirot is also on board.

book162.title: Night Shift
book162.author: Stephen King
book162.description: No, not the Lucy Dacus song! It's a collection of spooky Stephen King short stories instead. Perfect for enthusiasts of 80s horror.

book163.title: The Nightingale
book163.author: Hans Christian Andersen
book163.description: An emperor falls for a nightingale's song, but when a flashy mechanical bird appears, everyone forgets the real nightingale, and he flies away. A poetic tale that reminds us that no technology can truly capture the beauty of nature or one's talent.

book164.title: Nimona
book164.author: N. D. Stevenson
book164.description: Shapeshifter Nimona's plan was to become the sidekick to newly-termed villain Ballister. But when the heroes are not as goodhearted as everyone believed, that plan might have to change last-minute...

book165.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
book165.author: George Orwell
book165.description: A classic of dystopian social science fiction, for good reason. Totalitarianism, mass surveillance, and state oppression of nonconformity - 1984 has got them all.

book166.title: Non-Binary Lives; An Anthology of Intersecting Identities
book166.author: Various Authors
book166.description: Exploring what it means to be non-binary in the 21st century, this collection of essays shares how the gender identities of non-binary people across diverse backgrounds intersect and impact other aspects of their lives.

book167.title: Normal People
book167.author: Sally Rooney
book167.description: Follow Connell and Marianne as they grow up in Ireland, fall in love, struggle at school, and navigate their socioeconomic differences in this young romance novel.

book168.title: Northanger Abbey
book168.author: Jane Austen
book168.description: A young fangirl of Gothic novels has to learn that dark romance is not always so appealing in real life. A deliciously satirical Austen classic.

book169.title: The Notebooks of Malte Laurids Brigge
book169.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
book169.description: A deeply insightful near auto-biography, this book is bound to satisfy your urge for poetic prose but increase your urge for self-reflection - in the aristocratic, slightly depressing and very serious way. If you want to see death on every corner, this one's for you.

book170.title: Notes From A Small Island
book170.author: Bill Bryson
book170.description: After two decades in Britain, this American author isn't afraid to draw his conclusions about the small, weird, lovely island that had become his second home.

book171.title: One Of Us Is Lying
book171.author: Karen M. McManus
book171.description: When the Breakfast Club turns into a crime scene before detention is over, you know you'll be in for a thrilling, twisted mystery drama.

book172.title: One Piece; Volume 1
book172.author: Eiichiro Oda
book172.description: Sail the seas in this action-packed manga with Monkey D. Luffy and his crew, the Straw Hat Pirates! Follow Luffy as he goes on a journey to search for the treasure One Piece, and become King of the Pirates.

book173.title: Paper Towns
book173.author: John Green
book173.description: Margo is a mystery in human form, and Quentin would love nothing more than to solve her. The young adult novel for those who are looking to love for the answer.

book174.title: Paradise
book174.author: Toni Morrison
book174.description: Morrison herself wanted to call this book War . Her groundbreaking novel chronicles the catastrophic happenings taking place in an all-Black Oklahoma town and its counterpart, the Convent.

book175.title: Persuasion
book175.author: Jane Austen
book175.description: The 27-year-old Anne Elliot gets a second chance at love when her ex-fiance, Captain Frederick Wentworth, moves into her family's home. Another Austen classic that never gets old.

book176.title: Pet Sematary
book176.author: Stephen King
book176.description: Sometimes, dead is better... Because whatever came back from the grave no longer answers to "Heeere, kitty!". Another horror staple from Maine's biggest fan, Stephen King.

book177.title: Rambles in Germany and Italy; in 1840, 1842, and 1843
book177.author: Mary Shelley
book177.description: While Italy held many painful memories for Mary Shelley, she returned to the places she had once called home as a political ally in Italy's fight for independence.

book178.title: Red Dragon
book178.author: Thomas Harris
book178.description: The first novel in the Hannibal Lecter series introduces us to the infamous psychologist and cannibal, as he finds an unlikely ally in FBI profiler Will Graham. Absolutely gruesome and disturbing!

book179.title: The Red Virgin; Memoirs of Louise Michel
book179.author: Louise Michel
book179.description: In her memoirs, Louise Michel recounts her life as a revolutionary activist and educator, from the Paris Commune to her exile in New Caledonia. A true heroine of her time, the "Red Widow" affirms her anarchist, feminist, and anti-colonialist commitments.

book180.title: Red, White & Royal Blue
book180.author: Casey McQuiston
book180.description: The charming, cheeky, and slightly steamy rom-com where a First Son of America falls in love with a British crown prince, causing chaos, scandal, and plenty of swooning moments.

book181.title: Redwall; Book 1
book181.author: Brian Jacques
book181.description: Welcome to Redwall - An abbey that offers the sanctuary of good food, warm fires, and brave tales. This world is not without its dangers, but if a humble mouse can claim a fabled sword, they might just go down in song and legend!

book182.title: Richard Serra; Interviews, etc., 1970-1980
book182.author: Richard Serra
book182.description: The Man Behind the Masterpieces: Explore the life and artistic vision of the legendary sculptor and modern art icon in this series of interviews, presented alongside marvellous black-and-white photographs of his life's work.

book183.title: Romancero Gitano
book183.author: Federico García Lorca
book183.description: Eighteen romances where love and desire intertwine with violence and death. Lorca portrays the pride, resistance and suffering of the Romani people, their legends and traditions, revealing the hidden soul of Andalusia through rich symbolic poetry.

book184.title: Romeo and Juliet
book184.author: William Shakespeare
book184.description: No matter how many times you've seen it before, you will always be swept away by the passion and despair of these two lovers. And you might even be surprised by your own emotions.

book185.title: Salomé
book185.author: Oscar Wilde
book185.description: According to a reviewer of the play at its original performance, it is "an arrangement in blood and ferocity, morbid, bizarre, repulsive." Now, we might view Salomé as a symbol of modernity, a challenge and a revolt against a patriarchal Victorian society.

book186.title: Saving Danny
book186.author: Cathy Glass
book186.description: One of Cathy Glass's many fostering memoirs, this is the story of Danny, who comes into her care when his parents can no longer cope with his learning difficulties. It's a powerful testament to how a little love and patience can change a child's life.

book187.title: The Saviour Fish; Life and Death on Africa's Greatest Lake
book187.author: Mark Weston
book187.description: A captivating blend of travel writing and environmental reportage, this erudite work chronicles the author's life on remote Ukerewe Island in Lake Victoria, offering a profound perspective on ecological and cultural upheaval.

book188.title: Second Foundation
book188.author: Isaac Asimov
book188.description: Asimov's world-famous sci-fi epic continues as secrets unravel around the 14-year-old Arkady, alliances form in a war for the galaxy, and the true power of the Second Foundation is revealed.

book189.title: Shakespeare; The World as Stage
book189.author: Bill Bryson
book189.description: Unravel the enigmatic genius behind Shakespeare's words, as explained by Bill Bryson. A great and light-hearted introduction for every reader interested in the man behind the plays.

book190.title: Shatter Me
book190.author: Tahereh Mafi
book190.description: The first in a series of young adult novels, set in a dystopian world where one girl's touch is lethal. Will she finally escape the grasp of the government? And will she find love in the meantime?

book191.title: Shearwater; A Bird, an Ocean, and a Long Way Home
book191.author: Roger Morgan-Grenville
book191.description: Intertwining memoir, nature writing, and travelogue, this book chronicles the author's year-long adventure in pursuit of the longstanding object of his fascination: the impressive seabird known as the Manx Shearwater, or Puffinus puffinus !

book192.title: Shirley
book192.author: Charlotte Brontë
book192.description: Shirley is a traditional Brontë romance with a titular intelligent and headstrong heiress. Yet, the novel also deals with themes of economic struggles after the introduction of "labour-saving machinery". Sound familiar, anyone?

book193.title: Six of Crows
book193.author: Leigh Bardugo
book193.description: Six of Crows continues the dark YA fantasy series set in the "Grishaverse". Join the criminally talented Kaz Brekker as he gets together a crew of fellow teenage thieves to complete a dangerous task.

book194.title: Sky Island
book194.author: L. Frank Baum
book194.description: From Baum's much lesser known series of children's fantasy, Sky Island takes Trot, Button Bright, and Captain Bill to — you guessed it — an island in the sky. Illustrated by John R. Neill

book195.title: Skyward; (Book 1)
book195.author: Brandon Sanderson
book195.description: Humanity is trapped on a planet under attack by mysterious aliens. Spensa, living among them, dreams of joining the pilots defending humanity. Join her, as she fights for a place in flight school and faces the harsh reality of war.

book196.title: Slaughterhouse-Five
book196.author: Kurt Vonnegut
book196.description: Billy Pilgrim travels back and forth in time due to his post-war psychological trauma. Vonnegut combines his own experiences as an American soldier in 1945 Dresden with science-fictional elements to create one of the most revered anti-war novels of all time.

book197.title: Small Spaces; (Book 1)
book197.author: Katherine Arden
book197.description: With little more than ominous advice and stories of "the smiling man," Ollie and her classmates find themselves in a chilling race for survival when their bus breaks down on the way home from a field trip in this spooky series starter.

book198.title: Snow Crash
book198.author: Neal Stephenson
book198.description: Hiro Protagonist (yes, that's really his name) is a hacker and pizza delivery driver in a dystopian, futuristic America. who comes across a very dangerous data file in the Metaverse.

book199.title: Stories of Your Life and Others
book199.author: Ted Chiang
book199.description: A collection of eight marvellous science-fiction short stories, asking the question that speculative fiction always asks best: "what if?"

book200.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
book200.author: John Green
book200.description: Turned from a podcast into John Green's first non-fiction book, the writer rates various phenomena of the age of human intervention in nature on a scale of 1 to 5 stars.

book201.title: Antigone
book201.author: Sophocles
book201.description: The tale of a sister who will fight to honour her brothers after their death, no matter the cost. A tragic play about the strength of familial love and the consequences of defiance.

book202.title: Antony and Cleopatra
book202.author: William Shakespeare
book202.description: A tragic play set during the founding of the Roman Empire in 30 BC. Bask in the hot mess of a relationship between Egyptian Queen Cleopatra and Roman General Mark Antony.

book203.title: Anxious People
book203.author: Fredrik Backman
book203.description: An apartment showing becomes a hostage situation when a bank robber walks in. The catch: no one knows their identity! As the pressure builds, a collection of perfect strangers confess their deepest fears in this tender, mysterious, and furry story.

book204.title: The Autograph Man
book204.author: Zadie Smith
book204.description: Alex-Li Tandem is a mess. He makes his living by selling celebrity autographs, drinks too much, cheats on his girlfriend, and is hunting down an American actress whose last film came out in the 1940s.

book205.title: The Bad Beginning; (A Series of Unfortunate Events)
book205.author: Lemony Snicket
book205.description: When three siblings are suddenly orphaned, they have to live with their strange relative, Count Olaf. The failed actor wants to secure the family fortune for himself, but Violet, Klaus, and Sunny might stop him yet.

book206.title: Bait and Witch; (Witch Way Librarian Mysteries #1)
book206.author: Angela M. Sanders
book206.description: Josie expected to lie low in Wilfred, Oregon for a bit when she took a job as the small town's only librarian. She didn't expect latent magic powers, a fight to save the library from being torn down, or finding a body in the woods, but has to tackle all three head-on.

book207.title: Baking with Kim-Joy; Cute and Creative Bakes to Make You Smile
book207.author: Kim-Joy
book207.description: 40 recipes from the sunshine-filled Great British Bake Off finalist. If your desserts don't make your friends squeal with delight, are they even treats? This cookbook includes colourful instructions for making llama cookies, panda-madeleines, and choux bun turtles.

book208.title: The Ballad of Jacquotte Delahaye
book208.author: Briony Cameron
book208.description: Get ready for a pirate adventure following Jacquotte's rise to the captaincy. Join her, her friends, and the woman she falls in love with in this epic tale of overcoming hardships and empowerment

book209.title: The Bar Code Tattoo; (Bar Code #1)
book209.author: Suzane Weyn
book209.description: Everyone’s getting the bar code tattoo. When Kayla decides not to, her life as she knows it is thrown upside down and she finds herself on the run and wondering what exactly is the bar code tattoo – and why does everyone need one – in this YA sci-fi dystopia.

book210.title: Barmy British Empire; Horrible Histories
book210.author: Terry Deary
book210.description: History of the British Empire is full of horrible people and horrible deeds. Find out how a war started when a Brit was sitting on a stool and who wore a necklace made of human skulls in this not-so-horribly-boring history book!

book211.title: Baroque
book211.author: John Rupert Martin
book211.description: Aptly titled, Baroque covers the Baroque period of art and antiquity in Europe. There are 226 illustrations to go along with the drier descriptions, but if you read carefully, you'll become an amateur expert on the Baroque! How's that for a party trick?

book212.title: The Battle of the Labyrinth
book212.author: Rick Riordan
book212.description: Percy Jackson and his friends must enter the Minoan labyrinth to continue their godly quest and fulfil another prophecy in this fourth entry in the Olympian fantasy series.

book213.title: Battle Royale
book213.author: Koushun Takami
book213.description: Teens trapped on an island in a fight to the death? No, not that one! Junior high school students are forced to kill each other by a fictional, fascist Japanese government. The original novel has a powerful political message.

book214.title: Beartown; Book 1
book214.author: Fredrik Backman
book214.description: Beartown's last ember of hope lies in the success of its youth hockey league. When a scandal breaks involving the star player and the manager's daighter, each town member must choose whether they're on the side of justice, or the dream of a chance at finally winning.

book215.title: The Bell Jar
book215.author: Sylvia Plath
book215.description: Esther feels trapped in the confines of womanhood. After struggling with the expectations of marriage, sex, and work, and following multiple suicide attempts, she is hospitalised.

book216.title: The Big Sleep
book216.author: Raymond Chandler
book216.description: The most heteronormatively masculine, "hard-boiled", noir detective story you'll ever read. In which PI Philip Marlowe uncovers a criminal plot and seduces "damsels" left and right.

book217.title: The Binding
book217.author: Bridget Collins
book217.description: After a breakdown, young Emmett Farmer is apprenticed to a mysterious bookbinder. He learns to craft beautiful volumes that cage people's darkest secrets, yet one locked vault remains off-limits.

book218.title: Binti; (Book 1)
book218.author: Nnedi Okorafor
book218.description: Binti is the first of the Himba to attend the intergalactic Oomza University. On her way she confronts prejudice, war, and an forges a world-changing connection. A shining example of Africanfuturism

book219.title: Bird by Bird; Some Instructions on Writing and Life
book219.author: Anne Lamott
book219.description: The most difficult part of writing is just getting started! Author Anne Lamott gently guides the aspirational writer through each step of the writing journey. Learn how to observe, reflect, and give yourself plenty of grace through the process!

book220.title: Birdland
book220.author: Simon Stephens
book220.description: Watch the unravelling of Paul, a rock star at the prime of his career, in this cautionary play about fame and celebrity culture.

book221.title: Bleak House
book221.author: Charles Dickens
book221.description: A layered story about injustice and generosity, set amid the chaotic legal system of 19th-century London. The fortunes of many lie in the outcome of a twelve-year legal dispute. While lawyers quibble, drama, mystery, and tragedy unfold in the characters' daily lives.

book222.title: The Blind Assassin
book222.author: Margaret Atwood
book222.description: Stories within stories intertwine in this gripping tale as Iris Chase looks back on decades of her life. She recalls her childhood, her sister, her failed marriage, a world war... and reveals many secrets along the way.

book223.title: Blithe Spirit
book223.author: Noel Coward
book223.description: When a seance goes hilariously wrong, novelist Charles finds himself haunted by the ghost of his first wife, Elvira. Jealous of his new wife, Elvira acts out in desperation to keep Charles with her. A slapstick onstage farce of ghostly proportions!

book224.title: The Bluest Eye
book224.author: Toni Morrison
book224.description: This Morrison novel does not shy away from dealing with the devastating and harrowing consequences of the violence and abuse that were (and are still) inflicted upon young Black girls.

book225.title: Blurb Your Enthusiasm: A Cracking Compendium of Book Blurbs, Writing Tips, Literary Folklore and Publishing Secrets
book225.author: Louise Willder
book225.description: You pick up a book. What next? Maybe you read the hook on the back cover, the flaps, and the glowing blurbs authors give one another 'Astonishing!'... Did they even read it? Learn the humour and history behind the text outside of books! As meta as it gets.

book226.title: Body in the Library; Miss Marple  #2
book226.author: Agatha Christie
book226.description: The body of a young woman is found in the library at the Bantry estate. Before the police question the neighbours, Mrs Bantry suggests they consult Miss Marple, a silver-haired woman with a keen ear for village gossip and a keen eye for human nature.

book227.title: Book of Azrael
book227.author: Amber V Nicole
book227.description: He was a God; she was a demon—can I make it any more obvious? A true enemies to lovers and all the way back again, with her being the morally grey naughty one for a change.

book229.title: The Canterville Ghost
book229.author: Oscar Wilde
book229.description: Wilde's first published story is a classic ghost tale with lots of humour. Because what could be more fun than a bold American family moving into an estate haunted by an English aristocrat?

book230.title: Caps for Sale; A Tale of a Peddler, Some Monkeys and Their Monkey Business
book230.author: Esphyr Slobodkina
book230.description: A classic picture book about the dangers of taking naps under trees filled with monkeys. Hilarious and repetitive, what every child wants.

book231.title: The Cask of Amontillado
book231.author: Edgar Allan Poe
book231.description: Edgar did it again, a short story whose gruesome nature will linger much longer on your mind.

book232.title: The Color Purple
book232.author: Alice Walker
book232.description: A striking epistolary novel that continuously insists on the solidarity, friendship, and romantic love between women of colour, even in the face of the greatest adversities.

book233.title: The Colour of Magic; Discworld #1, Rincewind #1
book233.author: Terry Pratchett
book233.description: Wow! Is this that famous inn where all barbarians and adventurers get drunk and fight? As a wizard, Rincewind studied forms of intelligence that can be found in many alternate realities. Yet this tourist in Ankh-Morpork is a curious case in terms of intelligence.

book234.title: The Comedy of Errors
book234.author: William Shakespeare
book234.description: This play might be less deep than what we are used to from Billy S., but the slapstick, puns, mishaps, and chaos could make any modern audience laugh.

book235.title: The Comfort Book
book235.author: Matt Haig
book235.description: Matt saved all the little pieces of encouragement that kept him going, and put them in this book. This self-help book is an invitation to reflect and rebuild your hope. Take what you need!

book236.title: The Complete Father Brown
book236.author: G.K. Chesterton
book236.description: Father Brown is an English crime-solving priest with a sympathetic ear and sharp insight into human nature. This collection comprises 49 cases featuring the beloved cassock-wearing, bicycle-riding detective in the fictional village of Kembleford.

book237.title: The Complete Illustrated Encyclopedia of Birds of the World; A Detailed Visual Reference Guide To 1600 Birds And Their Habitats, Shown In More Than 1800 Pictures
book237.author: David Alderton
book237.description: Discover your environment one chirp, tweet or whistle at a time with this extremely detailed and very specific encyclopaedia. Do you really need more information than the title?

book238.title: The Complete Peanuts; 1993-1994
book238.author: Charles M. Schultz
book238.description: This collector's edition series compiles all 50 years of Peanuts comic strips published in newspapers from 1950 to 2000. Each volume contains two years of Charlie Brown and Snoopy's adventures to make you laugh and break your heart.

book239.title: The Complete Robot
book239.author: Isaac Asimov
book239.description: Sixty-two years after the first published instance of the word 'robot', Asimov collects his science-fiction short stories about the industrious automatons in this series.

book240.title: The Crucible
book240.author: Arthur Miller
book240.description: Did you dance with the devil last night? A critique of McCarthyism in the 1950s, this play uses the 1692 Salem witch trials to show how theocracy and personal vindictiveness are dangerous breeding grounds for hysteria-induced persecution.

book241.title: The Cruel Prince
book241.author: Holly Black
book241.description: Jude is a mortal living in the fae realm and is constantly tormented by the High Court. Worst of all is the youngest prince. But can she stand up to him without being roped into the intrigue of the palace?

book242.title: Crying in H Mart
book242.author: Michelle Zauner
book242.description: A heartfelt memoir from the artist behind Japanese Breakfast. Michelle writes about how grief sent her back to her Korean heritage for grounding and comfort, including the dishes she used to share with her mother.

book243.title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
book243.author: Mark Haddon
book243.description: Christopher might be only 15, but he notices things that others don't. When his neighbour's dog is suddenly killed, he wants to know what happened. This novel is unique in its use of maps, pictures, and diagrams!

book244.title: Cyrano de Bergerac
book244.author: Edmond Rostand
book244.description: A 19th century romcom—Cyrano, a skilled wordsmith, fears confessing his love to Roxane due to his large nose. Instead, he gets another man to woo Roxane in his place by giving her the love letters Cyrano writes. A tragicomedic play written entirely in poetic verse.

book245.title: The Decoration of Houses
book245.author: Edith Wharton
book245.description: Edith Wharton only became a writer at 40, and besides her many novels, she also wrote books on design, travel, and culture. At 60, she was the first woman to win a Pulitzer for Fiction. It is never too late to begin.

book246.title: The Dispossessed
book246.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
book246.description: Are YOU looking for feminist, anarchist sci-fi? I'm told Le Guin's Hainish Cycle is the place to start. While this book is technically the fifth book in the series, it is also the first in the chronology. Confusing, I know.

book247.title: The Duke and I
book247.author: Julia Quinn
book247.description: London's high society loves Daphne. Yet none of the eligible gentlemen are courting her so far. Can the brooding Duke of Hastings, who has no interest in marriage or society, help her raise her reputation?

book248.title: The Essential Rumi
book248.author: Rumi, transl. by Barks & Moyne
book248.description: The poetry and philosophy of the 13th-century Persian scholar known as Rumi have been among the most influential works in history.

book249.title: Eugene Onegin
book249.author: Alexander Pushkin
book249.description: Tatyana loves Eugene. Eugene thinks she's boring. Later, he wishes he had acted differently. A suspenseful Russian novel in Verse with a large cast of characters and plenty of philosophy to chew on!

book250.title: Europe Through the Back Door; A Travel Skills Handbook
book250.author: Rick Steves
book250.description: Catch yourself thinking, "I could live here," on nearly every trip? Make the most of your time in Europe by acting like you already do . Let TV-famous travel guide Rick Steves teach you how to connect with locals, avoid scams, and have a stress-free trip.

book251.title: Eurydice
book251.author: Sarah Ruhl
book251.description: This play is a love story. Or is it? It's hard to tell, with all the forgetting. Try again: this is a maybe love story about Eurydice, who dies on her wedding day and is taken to the underworld. Orpheus is coming to rescue her, but Eurydice is starting to forget day by day.

book252.title: Evelina
book252.author: Frances Burney
book252.description: Evelina is a naive young woman who learns first-hand about the dangers of fashionable society. A sharply comedic painting of excess, love, and women's status in eighteenth-century London. A novel from one of Jane Austen's favorite authors!

book253.title: Eye of the Storm; (Reel Magic Series)
book253.author: Meridwen Tidewell
book253.description: After a wild storm haunts Bookstonbury's shores, four adventurous kids find a mischievous mermaid by an old shipwreck. Sneaking kelp tea and dodging nosy adults, they decode slippery clues to help her uncover something fishy hidden beneath the waves.

book254.title: The Eyes of Darkness
book254.author: Dean Koontz
book254.description: A year after her son's death, Tina begins seeing things... Did Danny really die in an accident? And who is trying to conceal the truth from her? A paranormal horror-thriller.

book255.title: The Fall of the House of Usher
book255.author: Edgar Allan Poe
book255.description: American Gothic at its finest. Much like their protagonists, you will never be quite the same after diving into these deliciously dark stories.

book256.title: Famous Last Words
book256.author: Gillian McAllister
book256.description: Camilla's husband disappears, leaving a cryptic note. By noon, he's the gunman in a London hostage siege. As police close in, she's the only one who understands the message he left and the only person who can stop what comes next.

book257.title: The Fault in Our Stars
book257.author: John Green
book257.description: In the cancer support group her mother made her go to, 16-year-old Hazel meets Augustus. They share a love for books and metaphors and make each other rethink what it means to live, and what it means to die.

book258.title: The Glass Castle
book258.author: Jeannette Walls
book258.description: Journalist Jeannette Walls recounts her unstable childhood and the fraught relationship with her parents in this bestselling memoir.

book259.title: The God of Small Things
book259.author: Arundhati Roy
book259.description: The God of Small Things tells the dramatic story of twins from Kerala, India. They recall their childhood in 1969, as they grew up surrounded by family misery, political unrest, and forbidden love.

book260.title: The Great Gatsby
book260.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
book260.description: The glamorous tale of love and wealth that shaped the cultural imagination of "the roaring 1920s". Yet this story doesn't shy away from confronting the unknown dark sides of the "American Dream".

book261.title: The Handmaid's Tale
book261.author: Margaret Atwood
book261.description: A dystopian tale that imagines a totalitarian state in which the majority of women have been stripped of their freedom and reproductive rights to serve a Christian fundamentalist elite of men and their wives.

book262.title: The Happy Prince and Other Tales
book262.author: Oscar Wilde
book262.description: A charming collection of illustrated children's tales written by the famous Irish playwright. Also includes The Nightingale and the Rose , The Selfish Giant , The Devoted Friend , and The Remarkable Rocket .

book263.title: Hard Times
book263.author: Charles Dickens
book263.description: Meet Bouderby and Gradgrind, two men of industry. Their flawed views on life are evident in the outlooks of three children: Louisa, Thomas, and Cecilia. A comedic romance set amid the smoggy circus of mid-19th-century industrial society.

book264.title: Hatchet
book264.author: Gary Paulsen
book264.description: A 13-year-old boy named Brian gets stranded in the Canadian wilderness and has to survive with nothing but the damaged supplies from the plane wreck. Alone, but with the luck of the young, Brian takes on the great outdoors and learns he's not half bad at hunting.

book265.title: The Hidden Staircase; (Nancy Drew #2)
book265.author: Carolyn Keene
book265.description: Join the clever teenage detective Nancy Drew as she solves the mystery of a mysterious haunting. A detective story for all ages.

book266.title: The Hunger Games
book266.author: Suzanne Collins
book266.description: The twelve districts of Panem are barely held under control. To keep them from revolting, children from each are chosen for gladiator-like games. There can only be one survivor, so Katniss can't let her little sister be picked.

book267.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
book267.author: Oscar Wilde
book267.description: A hilarious and clever tale and a must-read for any fans of the Irish writer. A play that satirises Victorian society, from the author who ruffled many societal feathers.

book268.title: The Invasion; (Animorphs #1)
book268.author: K. A. Applegate
book268.description: Only 90s kids will remember wanting the ability to spontaneously transform into an animal. But be careful, because aliens are trying to infiltrate Earth and, if you don't change back, you might get stuck as a hawk forever!

book269.title: The Invention of Hugo Cabret
book269.author: Brian Selznick
book269.description: A mysterious tale about a young boy living in a Paris train station. With sparse pages of text, the story is told mostly through black-and-white illustrations, theatrically revealing tiny details of each scene-and Hugo's secret invention- one frame at a time .

book270.title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
book270.author: V.E. Schwab
book270.description: Addie Larue once made a deal with the devil. Now she wanders the world as a ghost, forgotten by everyone she meets. Follow Addie's journey to find meaning to her existence as she learns to leave her mark on the world, and discovers a man who can remember her name.

book271.title: The Invisible Man
book271.author: H. G. Wells
book271.description: A mysterious stranger appears at a village inn, causing chaos with the experiments he hides in his room. When he is discovered to have made himself invisible, a wild chase ensues. A thrilling classic of early science fiction.

book272.title: Is a River Alive
book272.author: Robert MacFarlane
book272.description: Robert MacFarlane travels from Ecuador's cloud-forests to India's wounded waterways and Canada's wild rivers, asking a radical question: What if rivers are alive? A luminous blend of travel, nature writing, and urgent environmental insight.

book273.title: The Island of Missing Trees
book273.author: Elif Shafak
book273.description: A tale of forbidden love and common roots set on the divided island of Cyprus in 1974. This story is told through multiple perspectives, shifting time, place, and species. The main narrator is a fig tree!

book274.title: The Last Battle; (Chronicles of Narnia)
book274.author: C.S. Lewis
book274.description: It is almost Judgment Day in Narnia. Like, actual Christian Judgment Day. Where Lion Jesus sends all of the good guys to heaven at the end. The metaphor is no longer subtle at all.
