book275.title: The Last Time I Lied
book275.author: Riley Sager
book275.description: Emma remembers the night her cabin mates snuck out... Some of it. The memory gaps still haunt her. Fifteen years later, she reluctantly returns to camp Nightingale, and it feels like someone's waiting for her to break. A chilling and twisty YA thriller!

book276.title: The Last Wish; (The Witcher)
book276.author: Andrzej Sapkowski
book276.description: A dark and dangerous story about fate, sorcery, and monstrous creatures. Accompany the Witcher, Geralt of Rivia, on his reluctant adventure, where he discovers curses, promises, and lovers.

book277.title: Life is Better When You Draw It
book277.author: Koosje Koene
book277.description: To draw what you see, you need to take in all the details of that moment, which makes you more aware of the moment you are living in and thus enjoy it more. This book is not here to teach you how to draw, but to inspire you to draw, nonprofessionally!

book278.title: The Lighthouse Mystery; The Boxcar Children #8
book278.author: Gertrude Chandler Warner
book278.description: Henry, Jessie, Violet, and Benny's days in a boxcar are behind them. Now they travel the world, solving mysteries nobody wanted their help with! This summer, the sibling are asleep in a lighthouse when their dog Watch wakes them, barking at something unseen.

book279.title: The Lightning Thief; (Percy Jackson #1)
book279.author: Rick Riordan
book279.description: In this tale of greek mythology, friendship and mediocre paternal figures for the ages, our young protagonist has to go on a mythic roadtrip to retrieve a stolen artifact or face Zeus's wrath.

book280.title: Little Lord Fauntleroy
book280.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
book280.description: Cedric, a middle-class American boy, learns he's heir to an English earldom. In the 1880s, this book popularized a trend in boys' fashion and set a legal precedent when the author insisted on compensation for theatrical adaptations of her work! Show me the money!

book281.title: The Little Prince
book281.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
book281.description: An enchanting tale of love, loss and an adventurous little prince who explores the universe and his own feelings. One sees clearly only with the heart . A must read for all ages.

book282.title: The Lorax
book282.author: Dr. Seuss
book282.description: A furry creature speaks for the trees and shows us how capitalism is destroying nature. Don't be fooled by the clever rhymes, this children's book is a razor-sharp critique and hard-hitting warning.

book283.title: The Lost Symbol
book283.author: Dan Brown
book283.description: Once again, symbologist Robert Langdom has to decode the secrets of old to save his mentor. This time in Washington D.C., there are undiscovered mysteries waiting for him.

book284.title: The Lost Words; A Spell Book
book284.author: Robert Macfarlane & Jackie Morris
book284.description: Gone are the days when children's alphabets began with A for Acorn , B for Butterfly and C for Caterpillar . But in this book of spellbinding poetry and enchanting illustrations, the magical words of nature, travel, and animals are restored into our lives.

book285.title: The Love Hypothesis
book285.author: Ali Hazelwood
book285.description: To convince her friends that she is over her ex, PhD student Olive convinces her young professor Adam to start a fake relationship. An example of fanfiction turned published book at its best.

book286.title: Lysistrata
book286.author: Aristophanes
book286.description: A delightfully devious play demonstrating the power of women and shared protest through unconventional means. Will the booty be too strong to resist for Lysistrata and her friends? Or will they bring an end to the Peloponnesian War?

book288.title: Madeline
book288.author: Ludwig Bemelmans
book288.description: Follow the adventures of 7-year-old Madeline in this illustrated children's book set in picturesque Paris. Spirited and brave in signature yellow, she navigates boarding school alongside her friends. A children's classic, loved throughout time, with memorable rhymes.

book289.title: The Magic City
book289.author: Edith Nesbit
book289.description: Out of discontent with his new life, young Philip builds a city out of his toys, books, and game pieces. Next thing he knows, he appears in a life-size version of it, populated with people who need his and Lucy's help.

book290.title: The Magic World
book290.author: Edith Nesbit
book290.description: This collection contains twelve beautiful and poetic short stories for children, including tales of talking animals, monarchs, fairies and beasts, and magical worlds.

book291.title: The Maid; Molly the Maid #1
book291.author: Nita Prose
book291.description: The first book in a mystery series with a lovable, neurospicy protagonist at its heart. Molly loves her job cleaning rooms at Regency Grand Hotel, but her gullibility makes her both an unreliable narrator and the perfect suspect for a murder mystery!

book292.title: The Martian Chronicles
book292.author: Ray Bradbury
book292.description: This classic sci-fi short-story cycle chronicles the exploration and settlement of Mars by the U.S. in the far and distant future of 2030. Bradbury explores militarism, genocide, oppression, and censorship from his post-war perspective.

book293.title: The Martian
book293.author: Andy Weir
book293.description: Astro-botanist Mark Watney is left behind on Mars after his crew narrowly escaped a dust storm. Alone and without supplies, the incorrigible optimist has to improvise in order to survive.

book294.title: The Massacre of Mankind
book294.author: Stephen Baxter
book294.description: Following on from the events in the War of the Worlds, the world has relaxed, safe in the knowledge of how to defeat the Martian Menace. But how should they be? London is a totalitarian dystopia, and nobody is as prepared as they should be...

book295.title: Maybe You Should Take to Someone; A Therapist, Her Therapist, and Our Lives Revealed
book295.author: Lori Gottlieb
book295.description: Lori Gottlieb is a therapist who needs therapy. As she tells the stories of her (nameless) patients, she recognizes themes in common with her own self-talk. A funny and hopeful memoir about our shared desires and capacity for change.

book296.title: The Maze Runner
book296.author: James Dashner
book296.description: Thomas wakes up among other teenagers in the centre of an ever-changing maze without his memories. He soon learns that all they can do to survive is to try and escape by any means necessary.

book297.title: The Murder at the Vicarage
book297.author: Agatha Christie
book297.description: A quaint village, a nosy vicar and a most sinister murder. Join Miss Marple, the Queen of Crime, on a typical English murder mystery, full of exaggerated characters and dry wit.

book298.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd (Hercule Poirot Series)
book298.author: Agatha Christie
book298.description: This famous whodunnit harbours a twist you might not see coming. As detective Hercule Poirot leaves retirement to review the crime scene, all signs point to a locked room that no one could have gotten into.

book299.title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
book299.author: Agatha Christie
book299.description: A book of many beginnings. The start of Christie's career as a prolific crime novelist. The first appearance of beloved Belgian detective Hercule Poirot. And a first in a long series of brilliant and suspenseful whodunnits.

book300.title: The Mysterious Benedict Society; The Mysterious Benedict Society #1
book300.author: Trenton Lee Stewart
book300.description: Four children pass a series of curious tests to qualify for an undercover operation. Their mission: find out what's happening at the Learning Institute for the Very Enlightened. Contains buckets of friendship, weird inventions, and adventure!

book301.title: The Namesake
book301.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
book301.description: Born in America to Indian parents, but named for a Russian author, it's no wonder that Gogol's life is marked by identity crisis. The moving novel The Namesake presents a portrait of Gogol and his immigrant family, exploring the challenges and relationships that come with evolving cultural values.

book302.title: Nana; Volume 1
book302.author: Ai Yazawa
book302.description: When two young women with the same name become roommates, they also become allies in the pursuit of romance and punk rock dreams. This iconic manga series promises love, drama and a sense of fashion that can't be beat.

book303.title: The Napoleon of Notting Hill
book303.author: Gilbert K. Chesterton
book303.description: In this alternate universe, successors of the Throne of England are chosen through random selection. And while the newest king fails to take his position seriously, one inhabitant of Notting Hill upholds his whimsical decisions with vigour.

book304.title: Nation
book304.author: Terry Pratchett
book304.description: Mau is the only member of his nation since a huge wave destroyed his village and wiped out his tribe. Now all alone, this boy defies death and demands answers: Why did the gods let this happen to the elders? Who will judge whether he becomes a man or remains a boy?

book305.title: Nature; Encyclopedia of Discovery
book305.author: Various Authors
book305.description: Discover the wonders of the natural world, from plants and animals to volcanoes and outer space. The immersive illustrations and diagrams make learning a delight for all ages.

book306.title: The Neverending Story
book306.author: Michael Ende
book306.description: When a little boy hides in the attic with a strange book, an exciting adventure begins in the book's fantasy world. A story about escapism and imagination for all of us who enjoyed hiding in our books.

book307.title: Nevermoor; The Trials of Morrigan Crow (Nevermoor #1)
book307.author: Jessica Townsend
book307.description: Cursed to die on her 11th birthday Morrigan is instead whisked away to a world she never knew existed to compete for membership in a secret society/ Sure, it's a preferable fate - but that doesn't mean it'll be easy!

book308.title: The New Encyclopedia of British, European & African Birds
book308.author: David Alderton
book308.description: This illustrated guide is a perfect companion for birdwatching, a scientific encyclopedia to start learning about birds and a source of inspiration for a birdwatching trip in Europe or Africa!

book309.title: New Hampshire
book309.author: Robert Frost
book309.description: A collection of poems and first Pulitzer Prize winning work by Robert Frost. His work is best known for its somber tone and descriptions of nature. Contains highly influential poems such as Fire and Ice and Nothing Gold Can Stay .

book310.title: The Outsiders
book310.author: S. E. Hinton
book310.description: Written by the author when she was still a teenager herself, this coming-of-age novel is known for dealing with the socio-economic struggles of White American working-class teenagers and the "greaser" gangs they formed.

book311.title: The Passage
book311.author: Justin Cronin
book311.description: The test subjects of a virus experiment develop strong physical and psychic abilities which cannot be controlled. The virus is spread and 90 years later, only a few colonies survive. One of them encounters the strange Amy...

book312.title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
book312.author: Stephen Chbosky
book312.description: Charlie doesn't fit in anywhere at his new school. He grapples with grief and flashbacks to his aunt's death. But two seniors take him under their wing, and Charlie experiences all the joy and despair of growing up.

book313.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
book313.author: Oscar Wilde
book313.description: The Narcissus myth of the Victorian times, Wilde's novel is a wonderfully Gothic exploration of the values of beauty, sensuality, and hedonism in their opposition to morality and social norms.

book314.title: A Place to Hang the Moon
book314.author: Kate Albus
book314.description: William, Edmund, and Anna need a guardian, so they slip into a crowd of evacuating London children, hoping to find a home. Nora, a friendly librarian, is the target of local gossip because of her German husband. But she has plenty of books, and makes a mean hot cocoa!

book315.title: The Poems of Emily Dickinson; Volume II
book315.author: Emily Dickinson
book315.description: A comprehensive collection of poetry written by a woman who never received much recognition for her work while she was alive.

book316.title: The Ramayana
book316.author: Valmiki
book316.description: This epic folk-tale was first composed around 300 BCE and was hugely influential on storytellers of later eras. Discover a modernised version and dive into heroics, battles with demons, and philosophical and spiritual wisdom.

book317.title: The Raven
book317.author: Edgar Allan Poe
book317.description: Once upon a dreary midnight, our protagonist is haunted by a raven, in this beautifully painfull poem about love and loss. Warning, it might leave you pondering weak and weary.

book318.title: The Sea of Monsters; (Percy Jackson #2)
book318.author: Rick Riordan
book318.description: Mythical monsters, cursed cruise ships and unexpected friends accompany our Olympian teenagers in this divine sequel to the fantastic Percy Jackson series.

book320.title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
book320.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
book320.description: This historical drama follows Evelyn Hugo, an old Hollywood star, as she prepares her spicy tell-all biography, full of highs and lows, love and tragedies.

book321.title: The Seven Lamps of Architecture
book321.author: John Ruskin
book321.description: This dry essay is a must-read for fans of gothic revival and a fun insight into the minds of 1800s mid-century architects. If you've ever wondered how architects 200 years ago contemplated their craft, this one's for you.

book322.title: The Shining
book322.author: Stephen King
book322.description: A haunted hotel, a writer with writer's block, his fraught marriage, and the creepiest children in literature. What could possibly go wrong?

book323.title: The Silence of the Lambs
book323.author: Thomas Harris
book323.description: A chilling thriller that won't let you go. Follow an FBI trainee as she struggles to cooperate with a cunning and cannibalistic psychopath to catch another serial killer.

book324.title: The Silmarillion
book324.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
book324.description: Tolkien finally takes his time to write his own religious scripture about the creation of Middle-earth. Perfect for all closeted fantasy-theologians.

book325.title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
book325.author: Unknown & Simon Armitage
book325.description: In this epic 14th-century poem, a green knight on a green horse (do they eat green eggs and ham?) arrives at Camelot on Yuletide. He throws his glove, an open challenge to King Arthur's knights. Sir Gawain accepts the wager, but he has no clue what he's in for!

book326.title: Siren Queen
book326.author: Nghi Vo
book326.description: Magic weaves itself into every fibre of the Golden-Age, where survival isn't guaranteed, as magic binds those seeking fame to a future of blood, sweat, and sacrifices. In order to make it, Luli Wei may have to give up everything - including the women she loves - in this stunning historical fantasy.

book327.title: The Song of Achilles
book327.author: Madeline Miller
book327.description: A marvellous retelling of the timeless classical epos, the Iliad, that focuses on the things that really matter. Complicated parents, the merciless politics of war, and, of course, the greatest love story of them all.

book328.title: Sorcery and Small Magics; The Wildersongs Trilogy #1
book328.author: Maiga Doocy
book328.description: Leovander Loveage has a problem. His charms got mixed up, and now he's been cursed to obey any command by his academic rival, the sullen Sebastian Grimm. Now they have to find a counterspell, and fast, in this first book of this queer fantasy series!

book329.title: Soul Music; Discworld #16, Death #3
book329.author: Terry Pratchett
book329.description: This novel could be about sex and drugs and rock 'n roll, but it is about a rock band. Also, there is a troll in the band, and a dwarf, and a suspiciously elvish-looking guy. The medieval ears of Discworld's citizens will hear metal, DEATH metal, so to speak!

book330.title: The Soul of Man Under Socialism
book330.author: Oscar Wilde
book330.description: Wilde sharply outlines the economic realities of his time and prescribes humanistic socialism as a cure. What might have been a hot take today was instead published as an essay packed with stellar quotes in 1891.

book331.title: The Spear Cuts Through Water
book331.author: Simon Jimenez
book331.description: You sit in a theatre, eyes riveted on the stage, as a brutal yet hopeful tale of gods, magic, and queer love unfolds in front of you. In this gripping novel, Jimenez turns the reader into an audience and forces them along on a pilgrimage to end a dynasty.

book332.title: The Stand
book332.author: Stephen King
book332.description: A guttingly dark exploration of a bioweapon-turned-pandemic wiping out most of humanity, and the struggle of good vs. evil amongst the survivors left in its wake. Not for the faint of heart.

book333.title: The Story Girl; Book 1
book333.author: L.M. Montgomery
book333.description: Fourteen-year-old Sara Stanley is a born storyteller. Both kids and grown-ups are captivated by her tales. Bev and his younger brother Felix spend a summer full of stories with their new friend Sara, hanging on every word.

book335.title: The Tell-Tale Heart
book335.author: Edgar Allan Poe
book335.description: Ba-bump, ba-bump, ba-bump. You killed someone and now the investigators are here. Ba-bump, ba-bump, ba-bump. Surely they must hear it, too. How will Poe's delightfully chilling short story end?

book336.title: The Tempest
book336.author: William Shakespeare
book336.description: In this Shakespearean classic, a wizarding scholar is disposed of by his brother and forced to take a sabbatical on a desolate island. A play full of thundering monologues, magical confusions and romantic distractions.

book337.title: The Templars; The Rise and Spectacular Fall of God's Holy Warriors
book337.author: Dan Jones
book337.description: A faltering war in the Middle East. A band of elite knights ready to die for Christianity's holiest sites. A secret financial empire answerable to no king and a deadly conspiracy built on lies...

book338.title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
book338.author: Anne Brontë
book338.description: Gilbert is curious about Helen, the quiet woman who moved into Wildfell Hall with her young son. A gothic romance novel with femjnist themes. So ahead of its time that Anne's sister Charlotte hid it from publishers until after Anne's death.

book339.title: The Traitor Baru Cormorant; (The Masquerade #1)
book339.author: Seth Dickinson
book339.description: After her home is colonised by Falcrest, Baru vows to climb the political ranks and destroy the empire from within to free her people. The first in a hard fantasy series filled with political intrigue and lesbian yearning, with a twist ending that will break your heart.

book340.title: A Tramp Abroad
book340.author: Mark Twain
book340.description: An unserious, humorous, mix of real and fictional accounts of travel across Europe. Exaggerated events, his struggle with the German language, and other tales color his journey.

book341.title: The Travels of Marco Polo
book341.author: Marco Polo
book341.description: In this totally real travelogue from the 13th century, we follow the author's self-insert — conveniently named Marco Polo — on his legendary travels from Venice to Beijing.

book342.title: Wars of The Roses; The Fall of the Plantagenets and the Rise of the Tudors
book342.author: Dan Jones
book342.description: The Hollow Crown: 15th-century England-Five kings, endless war. Plantagenets rip themselves apart in the Wars of the Roses. Agincourt glory, Towton bloodbath, Richard III's murdered nephews...

book343.title: War and Peace
book343.author: Leo Tolstoy
book343.description: A hefty chonk indeed. A famous historical novel with a meandering plot between - you guessed it: war and peace. As much about choosing the right life partner as it is about the Napoleonic Wars.

book344.title: The War of the Worlds
book344.author: H. G. Wells
book344.description: One of the first instances of Martians invading Earth. How will humanity defend itself? A great example of the what if they did to us what we did to others kind of sci-fi horror.

book345.title: The Well at the World's End
book345.author: William Morris
book345.description: Turns out the brilliant poet and designer William Morris also wrote a Fantasy classic. This beautifully illustrated book follows a young adventurer in an action-packed world of fading magic.

book346.title: The Wilder Shores of Love
book346.author: Lesley Blanch
book346.description: An engaging account of four women from the nineteenth century who threw off their corsets and escaped their boring, conventional lives to find love and adventure on the wilder shores of the Middle East.

book347.title: Will You Love Me?; The story of my adopted daughter Lucy
book347.author: Cathy Glass
book347.description: In this two-part fostering memoir, Cathy Glass shares the story of Lucy's journey, told from the perspectives of both her birth mother and foster mother, revealing how their lives became intertwined.

book348.title: The Willows
book348.author: Algernon Blackwood
book348.description: This wonderfully twisted gothic horror classic follows two friends on a fateful canoe trip. Scary campsite encounters and weird nature—this otherworldly thriller will make you relieved to be in the comfort of your home.

book349.title: The Woman in White
book349.author: Wilkie Collins
book349.description: The young art teacher Walter Hartright finds himself entangled in a complicated family mystery. Will he find out the underlying secret that led to the tragedy? Be prepared for a twist in this spooky classic.

book350.title: Women Travel Solo; 30 Inspiring Stories of Adventure, Curiosity and the Power of Self-Discovery
book350.author: Various Authors
book350.description: Solo travel can be intimidating! This anthology will encourage you to book that trip. Read bout the experiences and personal revelations of 30 female solo travelers, complete with scenic photographs to encourage your wanderlust.

book351.title: Women, Race and Class
book351.author: Angela Y. Davis
book351.description: In this groundbreaking essay, Angela Y. Davis explores the intersection of race, class, and gender, and how these factors shape the experiences of women in society. A foundational text in intersectional feminist theory.

book352.title: Working Songs of Bookstonbury
book352.author: Edwin Kimble
book352.description: A collection of traditional shanties and sea songs by sailors and dockworkers around Bookstonbury harbour. Contains some old classics, as well as lesser-known local songs like The Net-Eating Shark and Even The Seagulls Like A Good Book .

book353.title: The Yellow Fairy Book
book353.author: L. B. Alleyne & A. Lang
book353.description: A collection of some of the most well-known fairytales of European history. The many folktales, from Icelandic to Ukrainian to Estonian to Greek, are translated and edited for all children to enjoy.

book354.title: Yellowface
book354.author: R.F. Kuang
book354.description: June steals Athena's novel and reinvents herself as a literary star, until the truth starts leaking through the cracks. A thrilling story of fame, fraud, and one very persistent ghost of a reputation.

book355.title: Theodora Hendrix and the Curious Case of the Cursed Beetle
book355.author: Jordan Kopy
book355.description: Theodora lives with her spooky family, Mummy the mummy, Dracula, and the rest of the Monstrous League of Monsters. Join her as she fights to protect her family against the threat of the MLM Mansion!

book356.title: There's A Ghost In This House
book356.author: Oliver Jeffers
book356.description: Tour a spooky little house with a friendly little ghost! This creatively printed children's book alternates from grayscale illustrations to transparent vellum pages, so the pale ghost appears to float through the pages.

book357.title: They Both Die at the End
book357.author: Adam Silvera
book357.description: Life's expiration date is non-negotiable in this heart-wrenching story of two teenage boys spending their last 24 hours together. A story of love, hope, and death.

book358.title: The Third Gilmore Girl; A Memoir
book358.author: Kelly Bishop
book358.description: From A Chorus Line to Gilmore Girls, Kelly Bishop has seen it all. Now she spills the stories: showbiz highs, Vegas lows, iconic roles, and the unforgettable people she met along the way. A lively, candid memoir from a legend.

book359.title: This Book Will Bury Me
book359.author: Ashley Winstead
book359.description: After her father's death, Janeway finds a vehicle for her grief and unanswered questions: true crime discussion boards. She'll do anything to chase down new leads on a cold case, but her new online friends are hiding dark secrets of their own. An unputdownable thriller!

book360.title: Titus Andronicus
book360.author: William Shakespeare
book360.description: Follow the worst of the Romans, as he does the worst things in the worst ways possible. An incredibly violent Shakespeare play, not for the faint of heart, filled with revenge, monologues, and pies.

book361.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
book361.author: Harper Lee
book361.description: A timeless story of justice and innocence in a small Southern town where a lawyer takes on a charged case amid the prejudices and tensions of Depression-era Alabama.

book362.title: To the Lighthouse
book362.author: Virginia Woolf
book362.description: The Ramsay family spends the summer on the Isle of Skye with a few of their guests. Among them, a young painter observes the tensions and relationships between the family members and how they change 10 years later.

book363.title: A Tomb With a View; The Stories and Glories of Graveyards
book363.author: Peter Ross
book363.description: Uncovering the histories of those lying in a place where time stands still. Peter Ross pays homage to the famous, the infamous, and the forgotten in graveyards across Britain and Ireland. A book for all the taphophiles out there!

book364.title: Treasure Island
book364.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
book364.description: A young boy finds himself in the possession of a pirate treasure map in this classic story of treachery and treasure that will have your kids dreaming of becoming a pirate.

book365.title: Tree Houses: Baumhäuser - Maisons Dans les Arbres
book365.author: Philip Jodidio
book365.description: This trilingual book shows that building tree houses is not just fun for children. Beautiful pictures and descriptions of 30 tree houses from around the world: From private dream homes to luxury restaurants to a cathedral.

book366.title: True Beauty; Volume 1
book366.author: Yaongyi
book366.description: After being bullied for her appearance in middle school, Jugyeong starts over with a new look. After mastering the art of makeup, none of her new friends know what her face really looks like. The first print of the popular Korean webtoon.

book367.title: True Crime Story
book367.author: Joseph Knox
book367.description: In 2011, 19-year-old Zoe Nolan left a party at her flat and disappeared. Seven years later, writer Evelyn Mitchell is investigating the missing girl. Troubled by her findings, Evelyn consults Knox, a crime writer. A thriller so stacked with evidence, it feels real.

book368.title: True Grit
book368.author: Charles Portis
book368.description: It's 1878, and fourteen-year-old Mattie wants vengeance . Tom Chaney took her father's life, his horse, and $150 in cash. Mattie convinces Rooster Cogburn, the toughest U.S. Marshal in the west, to accompany her in a manhunt across Indian territory.

book369.title: The Truth; Discworld #25, Industrial Revolution #2
book369.author: Terry Pratchett
book369.description: Hear ye, hear ye! Ankh-Morpork has just invented the newspaper, the so-called source of the Truth. They thought revealing the Truth about political corruption and magical intrigues would blow citizens' minds, but a funny-shaped fruit is all the readers talk about!

book370.title: Tuesdays with Morrie
book370.author: Mitch Alborn
book370.description: Over many meaningful conversations made during many Tuesday visits, the author reconnects with his dying college professor, Morrie. This short-but-moving memoir reflects on life's greatest questions.

book371.title: The Turn of the Screw
book371.author: Henry James
book371.description: A young governess slowly realizes the two children under her care are the target of the creepy ghosts who haunt the estate. The troubling part is that Flora and Miles seem perfectly fine with it. Worst job ever.

book372.title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
book372.author: Jules Verne
book372.description: In this steampunk classic, a group of scientists around Captain Nemo unexpectedly embarks on an unforgettable underwater adventure in the Nautilus .

book373.title: Twisted Love
book373.author: Ana Huang
book373.description: In romance, there is something for everyone. This book is for the crowd who hear "possessive asshole, and her brother's best friend" and swoon.

book374.title: The Unmaking of June Farrow
book374.author: Adrienne Young
book374.description: Eventually, each Farrow woman begins to see, hear, and smell things that aren't there, slowly unravelling their grip on reality. June is starting to see the signs. A mysterious novel about the doors we choose, and how those choices shape who we become and who we love.

book375.title: Unmasking Autism
book375.author: Devon Price
book375.description: This book shares the author's personal experience with Autistic masking, extensive research on the history of the topic, as well as actionable advice and exercises to encourage self-expression. A ground-breaking work on neurodiversity.

book376.title: The Unusual Suspects; The Sisters Grimm #2
book376.author: Michael Buckley, Peter Ferguson (Illustrator)
book376.description: Granny Relda tells Sabrina and Daphne the truth about their legacy. That classic book of fairytales? It's actually a casebook of magical crimes. Oh, and their new school in Ferryport Landing may have monsters. The second volume in the series of Fractured fairy tales.

book377.title: Unwitting Wisdom; An Anthology of Aesop's Animal Fables
book377.author: Helen Ward
book377.description: A collection of twelve of Aesop's  fables, brought to life with beautiful illustrations. Discover the allegories that have enchanted children over 2500 years.

book378.title: Upgrading and Repairing PCs
book378.author: Scott Mueller
book378.description: The definitive guide to everything PC-related. Scott really makes it sound easy—a book for PC repair enthusiasts and those who might want to upgrade all the way to an unbelievable 64 megabytes of RAM!

book379.title: Valperga
book379.author: Mary Shelley
book379.description: A historical novel set in the Middle Ages, by certified goth nerd Mary Shelley. Mirroring the struggles of women in Shelley's time, the female protagonist must choose between love and political liberty.

book380.title: Vera Wong's Unsolicited Advice for Murderers; Vera Wong #1
book380.author: Jesse Q. Sutanto
book380.description: A dead man in her tea shop? Vera Wong barely blinks. After all, who's better suited to solve a murder than a sixty year old tea connoisseur with weaponized mum-curiosity? The police don't stand a chance.

book381.title: Villainous Victorians; Horrible Histories
book381.author: Terry Deary
book381.description: Teachers may tell you Victoria's Britain was an exciting place, but it was also a time for cruelty and wickedness. Read on for all the vile facts about the villainous Victorians, peppered with horribly hilarious humour that will keep you turning pages!

book382.title: Villette
book382.author: Charlotte Brontë
book382.description: Lucy is hired as a governess in Villette, France, where she faces loneliness, illness, friendship, and eventually love. A novel famous for its plot twists, thanks to a narrator who frequently hides information from the readers.

book383.title: Violets Are Blue
book383.author: James Patterson
book383.description: In this thrilling and bloody case, Detective Alex Cross investigates another macabre murder with undeniable signs of vampires while being haunted by someone from his past.

book384.title: Watchmen; (Issue #12)
book384.author: Alan Moore
book384.description: In the world of Watchmen , superheroes emerged in the 1940s and altered history as we know it with their presence. Tune in for the twelfth and last issue of the iconic comic series.

book385.title: Watership Down
book385.author: Richard Adams
book385.description: A journey of rabbits to find a new home, where they'll have to outwit enemies, "allies," and what seems to be every single one of the Prince's Thousand Enemies, for even when you reach the end, you find it's not that simple.

book386.title: Where the Wild Things Are
book386.author: Maurice Sendak
book386.description: As a child, throwing a tantrum is fun and all, until you find yourself in the middle of a group of "wild things". This delightful classic is about the important things, like dancing in the moonlight and missing your mum.

book387.title: White Teeth
book387.author: Zadie Smith
book387.description: This postcolonial novel focuses on the friendship of two wartime friends, a Bangladeshi and an Englishman. The story about mixed families, clashing ideologies and activism comes to a dramatic conclusion.

book388.title: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?
book388.author: Edward Albee
book388.description: A play about two couples meeting for a late-night party that quickly deteriorates into snide jokes and volatile fighting as secrets from both couples are laid bare. A dark comedy criticising the American nuclear family and the pressures of social conformity.

book389.title: Wuthering Heights
book389.author: Emily Brontë
book389.description: The only novel Emily Brontë ever wrote, and it's a masterpiece! A haunting tale of love and abuse set amidst the austere Yorkshire moors.

book390.title: You've Reached Sam
book390.author: Dustin Thao
book390.description: When the 17-year-old Julie loses Sam, the shared future they imagined dies with him and everything changes. All she wants now is to hear his voice again when she calls his phone. And against all odds, it doesn't go to voicemail...

book391.title: By Train Through Spain
book391.author: Amerigo Marchesi
book391.description: Join this charming and colourful journey across Spain with Amerigo Marchesi as they hop on trains, capture stunning vistas and uncover fascinating hidden gems.

book392.title: Discovering the Greater Bookston Region
book392.author: Peter Spinner
book392.description: Join Peter Spinner as he looks for the well-kept hidden gems of the enchanting Greater Bookston Region. High-quality restaurants, cosy stays, endearing shops, and local events await!

book393.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 2
book393.author: Ash Axbridge
book393.description: Get ready for a mind-blowing journey through the wondrous world of knowledge! Volume 2 of Encyclopaedia Bookstonia: from D as in Detective Novels to J as in Japanese Manga.

book394.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 3
book394.author: Ash Axbridge
book394.description: Discover a world of knowledge and adventure in this thrilling third volume of Encyclopaedia Bookstonia. From K as in Knitting Instructions to O as in Omegaverse.

book395.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 4
book395.author: Ash Axbridge
book395.description: Another epic volume filled with knowledge and wonder! What else does this encyclopaedia series have in store? I'll tell you: Entries from P as in Philosophy to T as in True Crime.

book396.title: Encyclopaedia Bookstonia Vol. 5
book396.author: Ash Axbridge
book396.description: Vol. 5 of this encyclopaedia concludes our journey of learning, with the entries we've all been waiting for: U as in Unfinished Manuscripts to Y as in Yuri. (They forgot to print Z).

book397.title: The Encyclopedia of the Weird and Wonderful; Curious and Incredible Facts that Will Blow Your Mind
book397.author: Milo Rossi
book397.description: Our world and history is a complex and fascinating thing, and this collection of entertaining facts and stories helps humanize our past. From prehistory, ancient games, Pompeii, and more, each page holds an entertaining tale.

book398.title: Finding Optimism; The Future Is Good
book398.author: Liliane Renaud
book398.description: Liliane Renaud believes that, despite everything, the future must be bright. This solarpunk-inspired work is packed with thoughtful poems and practical insights to guide you through life's most difficult challenges.

book399.title: Herbcraft; The Power of Natural Healing and Hexing
book399.author: Star Ravenhunt
book399.description: Get ready to brew up some magic as Star Ravenhunt shares the secrets of herbcraft, from natural healing potions to delicious recipes to mischievous hexes.

book400.title: Here Be Dragons; (Welsh Princes #1)
book400.author: Sharon Kay Penman
book400.description: The first in a trilogy of Medieval Fantasy Romance follows the tale of Joanna - the illegitimate daughter of King John - as she finds herself choosing between loyalty and love.

book401.title: Historical Niche
book401.author: Terry Czernik
book401.description: This in-depth exploration of the Danelaw by a scholar of history promises sophisticated insights for anyone with an interest in 886–1066 AD in Northern England.

book402.title: HTML 1998; An Introdcution
book402.author: Hello Worldly
book402.description: Get ready to enter the digital world with this 90s guide to HTML (specifically 3.2), the language that powers the internet. Let's say "Hello, World!"

book403.title: In Search Of:; The Most Beautiful Islands In the World
book403.author: Je Hyun
book403.description: The newest entry in our In Search Of series: A marvellous view across stunning islands, where paradise awaits at every turn, even if you're on a budget.

book404.title: Just A Story: Why We Still Tell Fairytales
book404.author: Isabel Galvan
book404.description: Once upon a time... there was the captivating world of fairytales. Discover why these timeless tales continue to enchant and intrigue us in this cultural and anthropological study.

book405.title: Kitchen Rules For Your Family and You
book405.author: Mbwana Jones
book405.description: Spice up your family's kitchen adventures with this delightful guide. From cooking tips to family bonding, discover the recipe for a happy home!

book406.title: Know My Name
book406.author: Chanel Miller
book406.description: In the news, she was known only as Emily Doe. Chanel's experience, an example of the justice system failing the most vulnerable, went viral after her victim impact statement was posted on Buzzfeed. A powerful memoir told in uniquely beautiful prose.

book407.title: Living In Alaska
book407.author: Sioned Jones
book407.description: This chilling page-turner, based on Jones' true story, will take you on a wild journey through the frozen wilderness of Alaska, filled with heartbreak, resilience, and unexpected turns.

book408.title: The Long Unwinding Road; A Journey through the Heart of Wales
book408.author: Marc P Jones
book408.description: Come with Marc P Jones as he takes you through the beautiful green hills and valleys of Wales. Discover Wales' deep majesty and ancient history, with local voices at the fore.

book409.title: Medieval Carpentry
book409.author: Obu Henderson
book409.description: Woodworking tips and tricks from the days of knights and castles. Unearth ancient techniques and bring medieval craftsmanship back to life!

book410.title: Mesopotamian Buildings
book410.author: Ahmed Mansour
book410.description: Discover the awe-inspiring marvels crafted by ancient hands in this fascinating delve into Mesopotamian architecture. Join us on a journey through time!

book411.title: Physics 1908
book411.author: Kendra Conelli
book411.description: Discover the captivating world of physics through a historical journey that will tickle your brain and transport you to 1908.

book412.title: Round Luxembourg with Brooke
book412.author: Brooke Dixon
book412.description: Join rising Instagram star BrookeTravels on an adventure through Luxembourg as she explores, shares delicious recipes, and provides a refreshing take on travel and lifestyle.

book413.title: Round the World in Eighty Dishes
book413.author: Lesley Blanch
book413.description: A rich collection of dishes from around the world, each accompanied by its own travel anecdote that opens a fascinating window into a time long past.

book414.title: St. Bookston: The Myth, the Legend, the Truth
book414.author: H. A. Pennington
book414.description: The most brilliant writer and philosopher of his time. But who was he really? And why do we know so little about his life? Finally uncover the truth in this groundbreaking investigative biography.

book415.title: The Debvoir Family; A Success Story
book415.author: Kennedy Naybon
book415.description: Follow the triumphs and trials of a remarkable family, as the Debvoir clan shapes and is challenged by the very history of Bookstonbury.

book416.title: Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen
book416.author: Olympe de Gouges
book416.description: "Woman has the right to mount the scaffold, she must equally have the right to mount the rostrum [speaking platform]." French Revolutionary Olympe de Gouges flips the male-only Declaration of Human Rights, in this fearless and witty manifesto for gender equality.

book417.title: Top 50 Camper Van Destinations
book417.author: Tamir Ghasti
book417.description: From winding coastal roads to serene mountain retreats, this comprehensive camping guide unveils a collection of breathtaking landscapes and hidden gems.

book418.title: Topdog/Underdog
book418.author: Suzan-Lori Parks
book418.description: Booth wants to be as good at three-card monte as his older brother Lincoln, who's sworn off the hustling life. Money's tight, and Lincoln's honest work isn't going to get them far, as this one-room play explores the intersection of race, poverty, and brotherhood.

book419.title: Traditional Building Techniques
book419.author: Lohar Bishmal
book419.description: Have you ever looked at an old city's houses, castles and bridges and asked yourself: "How did they build that"? This book illustrates the greatest building techniques of all time and what we can learn from them today.

book420.title: A Clash of Kings
book420.author: George R. R. Martin
book420.description: The 2nd volume in the ASOIAF series continues to deliver the most heart-wrenching twists and tragedies of medieval fantasy: mysteries of parentage, magic, murder, war, and epic adventures all throughout the lands of Westeros.

book421.title: The Code Book; The Science of Secrecy from Ancient Egypt to Quantum Cryptography
book421.author: Simon Singh
book421.description: Crack codes, unravel secrets, and explore gripping historical mysteries. From ancient ciphers to World War II's Enigma, Singh invites you to learn cryptography and test your skills with real code-breaking exercises.

book422.title: A Court of Mist and Fury
book422.author: Sarah J. Maas
book422.description: Get ready for a sexy, epic and twisting book two in the ACOTAR series, where the immortal drama of the fae unfolds around haunted protagonist Feyre. Will she find the right side to stand with?

book423.title: The Cream Tea Killer
book423.author: Judy Leigh
book423.description: Amateaur sleuth Morwenna is looking forward to a bit of normality, until the local DJ she was supposed to be meeting washes up at the beach. Despite being dubbed The Cream Tea Killer , they are anything but sweet and it is up to Morwenna to unmask them.

book424.title: A Feast for Crows
book424.author: George R. R. Martin
book424.description: The war for the Iron Throne seems to have burned itself out to a truce... for now. But it wouldn't be A Song of Ice and Fire without some deceit, ambitious plotting, power struggles, and mysterious sorcery at work.

book425.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
book425.author: William Shakespeare
book425.description: Simple love triangles are for beginners. In this classic play, romantic entanglements involve four young, love-sick Greeks, fae royalty, enchantment spells, and a donkey, resulting in a comedy for the ages.

book426.title: Walden
book426.author: Henry David Thoreau
book426.description: Ever wanted to walk away from civilization, into the woods, and owe nothing to anyone but yourself? You'll find a friend in Henry David Thoreau. His record of simple living and contemplation of civil disobedience will fascinate nature-lovers and deep thinkers alike.

book427.title: A Walk in the Woods
book427.author: Bill Bryson
book427.description: The tale of two men in their forties, with countless blisters and a questionable map, on the Appalachian Trail. Get to know the area's history, ecology, and people in this hilarious exploration of the great outdoors.

book428.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
book428.author: Lewis Carroll
book428.description: Follow a curious girl as she tumbles down the rabbit hole, into a world filled with talking animals and puzzling adventures. A classic tale of nonsense and whimsy, illustrated by John Tenniel.

book429.title: All My Sons
book429.author: Arthur Miller
book429.description: Set in the Midwest after WWII, this play is a fragmented family drama and tragedy. A father and son, a forbidden romance, unpunished crimes, and a dark secret that threatens to tear the characters apart.

book430.title: All Out; The No-Longer-Secret Stories of Queer Teens throughout the Ages
book430.author: Various Authors
book430.description: An anthology of Queer historical fiction, telling captivating and emotive stories which take you on a journey through history. Experience a diverse range of identities, stories, and cultures in this vibrant expression of queer history.

book431.title: All She Was Worth
book431.author: Miyuki Miyabe
book431.description: How desperate is a person who steals another's identity? Detective Honma searches for his nephew's missing fiancée, unravelling grim crimes to uncover the true Shoko since the dead leave traces in the living.

book432.title: All Systems Red; The Murderbot Diaries #1
book432.author: Martha Wells
book432.description: Meet Murderbot, a SecUnit who recently hacked their governor chip. Too bad it keeps getting sent on planetary bodyguard contracts for the shady Company! All this android wants is space to have an existential crisis and binge-watch their favourite program.

book433.title: All Your Twisted Secrets
book433.author: Diana Urban
book433.description: Six high school teenagers meet up under false pretenses and are locked in a room with only one direction: before the hour is up, they must choose one person to die. Amidst the chaos that ensues, a second question rises: who did this to them?

book434.title: All's Well That Ends Well
book434.author: William Shakespeare
book434.description: Sometimes, a happy ending can be a woman getting the man she wanted, even if he's generally quite unpleasant. Shakespearean drama and confusion as it should be.

book435.title: Allegiant; Divergent #3
book435.author: Veronica Roth
book435.description: As the Factionless seize power, a new civil war threatens to destroy what remains of the shattered faction society. Tris, Four, and a handful of allies must venture beyond the barriers to save their city from self-destruction. How is the war going to end? And when?

book436.title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold
book436.author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
book436.description: In this heartwarming and thought-provoking story, a cosy cafe in Tokyo has a mysterious twist... Can you change the past, or will the coffee get cold before you do?

book437.title: Belinda
book437.author: Maria Edgeworth
book437.description: Belinda has aspirations beyond London's social season. Amongst the heroine's witty observations of eighteenth-century society, this novel also touches on the challenging issues of feminism, racism, and obsession. One of Jane Austen's favourite books!

book438.title: Beowulf
book438.author: Unknown, transl. by S. Heaney
book438.description: An Old English epos that still puzzles scholars to this day. Who can we credit for this poetic tale of a Scandinavian folk hero? When was it written? And how much does it tell us about our history?

book439.title: The Best Short Stories of O. Henry
book439.author: O. Henry, B. Cerf & V.H. Cartmell
book439.description: 38 tales from an American writer famous for surprise endings! Will Porter began writing short stories from prison in 1898. He later changed his name and started fresh in New York City. He wrote over 600 stories in his lifetime. Some aged better than others.

book440.title: Blood of Elves; (The Witcher)
book440.author: Andrzej Sapkowski
book440.description: After the success of previous short stories, the Polish fantasy series now takes off into its first novel, wherein the magically gifted Ciri must flee from her war-torn home, and comes under the protection of Geralt of Rivia.

book441.title: Blood, Sweat, and Pixels
book441.author: Jason Schreier
book441.description: Jason Schreier, documents how ten famous video games were developed by interviewing their developers retrospectively. These real stories of dedication, hope, suffering, and frustration reveal the intricacies of the game industry.

book442.title: The Blue Castle
book442.author: L.M. Montgomery
book442.description: When 29-year-old Valancy gets bad news from her doctor, she decides she’s ready to live. She’s done letting her family dictate how she spends her days, and she offers friendship to the townsfolk they despise. A romantic and hopeful novel about second chances.

book443.title: Blue Highways; The Travel Trilogy #1
book443.author: William Least Heat-Moon
book443.description: William set off on what would become a 13,000 mile journey by van, visiting the most overlooked small towns in America. His series of travel memoirs prove that it's not where you go, it's who you meet! Blue highways are back roads.

book444.title: Blue Sisters
book444.author: Coco Mellors
book444.description: After their sister’s death, three wildly different siblings return to New York to save their childhood home and face the truths they’ve long avoided. A moving, sharp story of grief, identity, and the ties that bind.

book445.title: Carrie
book445.author: Stephen King
book445.description: A classic of dark teen horror. High schooler Carrie White is mercilessly bullied by her peers and abused by her religious mother. But when an especially cruel prank is used to humiliate her, her latent telekinetic powers know no bounds.

book446.title: Case Closed; One and the Same? (Vol. 3)
book446.author: Gosho Aoyama
book446.description: When 17yo superstar detective Shinichi Kudo follows the wrong people, he's poisoned and turns back into a kid! Now as grade schooler Conan Edogawa, he still solves cases, this time on a cruise ship, in this famous whodunnit Manga series.

book447.title: Catching Fire
book447.author: Suzanne Collins
book447.description: The cycle established in the dystopian society of Panem continues. The brutal Hunger Games are held again, and traumatised Katniss and Peeta get no choice but to play along, and fight not only for their survival, but also for a revolution...

book448.title: Cats in Space... and Other Places
book448.author: Various Authors
book448.description: Love Cats? Love Spaces? You'll love this. Revel in feline supremacy while reading tales by the likes of Ursula Le Guin, Arthur C. Clarke and Anne McCaffrey. Approved by Freya!

book449.title: Caturday in Bookstonbury; Volume 2
book449.author: Luna Knight
book449.description: In this visual photographic history of Bookstonbury, Luna Knight documents the local feline population. From majestic longhairs to playful shorthairs and everything in between, take a gander and learn more about these adorable floofs.

book450.title: The Caucasian Chalk Circle
book450.author: Bertolt Brecht
book450.description: A play-within-a-play culminating in a trial to decide if a boy should go to the rich woman who gave birth to him or the maid who raised him. A piece of Epic Theatre which delivers political themes of justice, class inequality, and the aftermath of war.

book451.title: Cemetery Boys
book451.author: Aiden Thomas
book451.description: A trans teen determined to prove to his Latinx family that he’s a brujo tries to summon his cousin’s spirit to solve his death, but ends up instead with a ridiculously handsome ghost. A hauntingly cute paranormal romance and mystery perfect for spooky season.

book452.title: Chain-Gang All-Stars
book452.author: Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah
book452.description: For nearly three years, Loretta has fought and killed, hoping to win her own freedom. Told in multiple perspectives, this brutal dystopian novel highlights the horrors of the US prison system and society's obsession with reality entertainment.

book453.title: The Chalk Man
book453.author: C.J. Tudor
book453.description: In 1986, Eddie and his friends used chalk figures as a secret code—until it led them to a body. Now in 2016, these menacing figures have returned, and another murder ensues. Eddie must return to the past to uncover seething secrets and unearth the killer's identity.

book455.title: Crime and Punishment
book455.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
book455.description: Poverty and guilt drive a bright young man to a dark deed. How will he grapple with the consequences of his crime?

book456.title: Critical Hits; Writers on Gaming and the Alternate Worlds We Inhabit
book456.author: Various Authors
book456.description: An anthology of personal essays by multiple published authors exploring their relationship with video games that affected them deeply, Learn about the transformative world of games and how they shape our lives.

book457.title: The CRPG Book; Guide to Computer Role-Playing Games
book457.author: Collection
book457.description: This encyclopedia tells the history of computer role-playing games by listing all CRPG titles released up to 2020 in chronological order. You can see how games influenced each other and role-playing practices, both in digital and tabletop settings.

book458.title: Don Quixote
book458.author: Miguel de Cervantes
book458.description: A mad "knight" embarks on hilarious adventures with his faithful, not-so-bright sidekick in this classic satire.

book459.title: Don't Let the Forest In
book459.author: C.G. Drews
book459.description: A gothic high school, a haunted writer, a secretive artist. Andrew and Thomas must fight back the monstrosities born from the art they created, while their feeling for each other grow tangled and wild.

book460.title: Dune
book460.author: Frank Herbert
book460.description: An epic saga of intergalactic politics and precious resources, where one young man finds himself surrounded by inhospitable desert, and at the centre of a messianic prophecy.

book461.title: East of Eden
book461.author: John Steinbeck
book461.description: A retelling of Genesis set on California farmland in 1865. This complex novel centers on the timeless struggles of two families, exploring themes of rivalry, identity, and love.

book462.title: Edinburgh; Picturesque Notes
book462.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
book462.description: A travelogue told in a series of anecdotes with whimsical exaggerations that capture the author's view of his hometown circa late 1870s, in all its glories and infamies.

book463.title: The Eleventh Hour; A Curious Mystery
book463.author: Graeme Base
book463.description: Horace the elephant invites his friends to celebrate his eleventh birthday with a feast, only to discover that it has been eaten at the eleventh hour! Can you find the hidden messages and solve the mystery of who ate the birthday feast?

book464.title: Elsewhere; One Woman, One Rucksack, One Lifetime of Travel
book464.author: Rosita Boland
book464.description: Rosita reflects on the life-changing experiences and people she met on nine journeys, from a chaotic bus ride in Pakistan to a healing swim in Bali, carrying only a rucksack and a diary.  An emotion-filled collection of essays, both thrilling and heartbreaking.

book465.title: Fire & Blood
book465.author: George R. R. Martin
book465.description: Finally, an even more historical fantasy novel, from the world of Ice and Fire. Wherein all the messy relationships, wars, and secrets of the royal Targaryen dynasty are aired out.

book466.title: Frank Lloyd Wright
book466.author: Frank Lloyd Wright
book466.description: From prairie houses to the Guggenheim museum, this architect had range! This wonderful coffee table book is jam-packed with sketches and photographs for all architecture enjoyers.

book467.title: Frankenstein
book467.author: Mary Shelley
book467.description: Oh, to be 18 again, and write a masterpiece over a particularly cold and dark summer holiday, unknowingly laying the very foundation of our modern horror fiction. Wish that were me.

book468.title: Ghost Stories; From the Grave
book468.author: Collection
book468.description: Prepare to be chilled to the bone as you journey into the realm of the supernatural with this collection of eerie and haunting tales. With Dickens, Stoker, Wilde, and Poe, as well as new stories.

book469.title: Great Big Beautiful Life
book469.author: Emily Henry
book469.description: Two writers. One legendary subject. Alice wants her big break. Hayden wants everyone to leave him alone. Instead, they're trapped on an island competing for the same biography, juggling cryptic stores, ironclad NDAs, and an attraction neither of them requested.

book470.title: Great Expectations
book470.author: Charles Dickens
book470.description: A classic Dickens! Poverty, morality, smelly cities, and unjust austerity measures lead to a rags-to-riches extravaganza with a lot of heartbreak on the way. Oh, right, I forgot orphans.

book471.title: Heinemann Mathematics
book471.author: Scottish Primary Mathematics Group
book471.description: The classic textbook for everyone's favourite subject in school! Packed with all the greatest hits like arithmetic, trigonometry, and stochastics.

book472.title: How Winston Delivered Christmas; A Christmas Story in Twenty-Four-and-a-Half Chapters
book472.author: Alex T. Smith
book472.description: A brave little mouse sets off on a quest to deliver a lost letter to Father Christmas on Christmas Eve. This picture book is designed to be read as an Advent calendar, and includes activities for children impatiently counting down the days till Christmas.

book473.title: Howl, and Other Poems
book473.author: Allen Ginsberg
book473.description: There are nice poems, and then there are those tried by the law in an obscenity trial: Radical, honest, political, soft, holy. And life-changing. I much prefer the latter category.

book474.title: I Capture the Castle
book474.author: Dodie Smith
book474.description: Seventeen year-old Cassandra lives in the remnants of a castle with her eccentric family. Her 1934 journal is going strong, but her father's latest book is a work-in-procrastination, so money is tight. Maybe romance and a strategic prank can change their fates!

book475.title: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
book475.author: Maya Angelou
book475.description: Maya's childhood was one of prejudice, neglect, and violence. Adult Maya finds the keys to her cage of trauma through self-love, escaping to the embrace of good books and kind people. A tragic and inspiring autobiography from a resilient Black poet.

book476.title: I, Robot
book476.author: Isaac Asimov
book476.description: This set of nine delightful short stories imagine a world of robot and human colaboration and explores some interesting concepts within this framing. A foundational text of modern Sci-Fi, and a must read in the storebought version of the future we ended up in.

book477.title: If Beale Street Could Talk
book477.author: James Baldwin
book477.description: Tish and Fonny are engaged and expecting a child, when Fonny is jailed for a crime he didn't commit. Their families band together to try to clear his name. An emotionally devastating love story about racial prejudice and criminal injustice.

book478.title: If Tomorrow Comes
book478.author: Sidney Sheldon
book478.description: A thrilling mystery about a regular woman's descent into a life of crime. Betrayed by love and framed by the mafia, Tracy has to fight back to survive.

book479.title: Inkheart
book479.author: Cornelia Funke
book479.description: Pen and paper can bring characters to life, but what happens when they escape the page? The beginning of a fantastical and dangerous adventure into the world of a book, for all ages.

book480.title: Jane Eyre
book480.author: Charlotte Brontë
book480.description: This intimately narrated story of the winding life of Jane Eyre touches on many social issues present in Victorian England. Her story is frought with twists and hardships but ultimately leads to love.

book481.title: Jean Dubuffet
book481.author: Jean Dubuffet
book481.description: Explore the fascinating world of French artist, Jean Debuffet. Learn how he strived to thwart conventional standards of beauty in favour of more authentic and humanistic ways of image making.

book482.title: Henry VI, Part 1
book482.author: William Shakespeare
book482.description: Watch as personal squabbles, petty jealousy and Joan of Arc tear apart the English political system in this first part of Shakespeare's King Henry VI trilogy.

book483.title: Henry VI, Part 3
book483.author: William Shakespeare
book483.description: This final part of Shakespeare's King Henry VI trilogy focuses on the horrors that ensued during the Wars of the Roses as the nation is thrown into chaos and morality makes way for revenge.

book484.title: Richard II
book484.author: William Shakespeare
book484.description: Shakespeare's classic historical drama about the downfall of King Richard the Second, complete with scheming nobles and history-defining power politics.

book485.title: Legendborn; The Legendborn Cycle #1
book485.author: Tracy Deonn
book485.description: A magical story about black women and pain through generations. In this twist on King's Arthur's legend, Bree struggles to find out why she is the only one who can resist the effects of magic and how the secret order she infiltrates relates to her mother's death.

book486.title: Les Miserables
book486.author: Victor Hugo
book486.description: 19th-century Paris. A man running from the law just wants a chance to live his life. Injustice is everywhere. But resistance is brewing, and love is not far. Don't expect anyone to sing, or you'll be disappointed.

book487.title: Letters from Egypt; 1862-1869
book487.author: Lucie Duff Gordon
book487.description: After her diagnosis of tuberculosis, Lady Gordon travels to Egypt in hopes of improving her dwindling health. A compilation of her letters, detailing her account of life in Luxor, this is the story of an Englishwoman's immersion into Egyptian culture.

book488.title: Letters of Bookstonbury
book488.author: Allatheena Jeon
book488.description: After her grandmother's death, a quiet librarian inherits a mobile bookshop. She plans to sell it - until she finds a hidden compartment beneath the floorboards, with old, unsent letters addressed to people all over town, uncovering stories of love, loss, and hope.

book489.title: The Library Book
book489.author: Susan Orlean
book489.description: A journalist's engaging investigation into the 1986 fire at the Los Angeles Public Library. Part true-crime story, part essay on what libraries mean to us, and why the burning of books or libraries is so devastating

book490.title: The Long Way to a Small Angry Planet; Wayfarers #1
book490.author: Becky Chambers
book490.description: In this queer space opera, a rag-tag team of travelers take a dangerous job tunnelling a wormhole to a distant planet. The commission of a lifetime might not pay off, but the found-family in this sci-fi series sure does!

book491.title: Looking for Alaska
book491.author: John Green
book491.description: Boarding school is not what Miles thought it was gonna be. And neither is that girl he meets, Alaska. Together they search for the meaning behind last words, in this young adult story.

book492.title: Lord of the Flies
book492.author: William Golding
book492.description: A group of school boys is suddenly stranded on a remote island. Will they manage to survive without any grownups, or will they succumb to their darker instincts?

book493.title: A Man for All Seasons
book493.author: Robert Bolt
book493.description: This biographical dramatization follows the escalating conflict between Lor Chancellor Sir Thomas More and Henry VIII from 1529 to 1535. As Henry pushes political and religious buttons, More pushes back. A historical play that will leave you wanting more.

book494.title: Maria Stuart
book494.author: Friedrich Schiller
book494.description: A Tudor tale of power, betrayal, and queens. Witness the captivating drama and heart-wrenching decisions of a regal Mary, in this loveletter to Shakespearian plays by a legendary German playwright.

book495.title: Matilda
book495.author: Roald Dahl
book495.description: A mischievous little genius delights in books and uses her powers to outsmart nasty grown-ups. Will she make it through the school system in one piece?

book496.title: A Matter of Oaths
book496.author: Helen S. Wright
book496.description: When memory-wiped Rafe applies for a job on a random patrol ship, a world-changing space opera unfolds: space battles, secret identities, queer romance, and VR tech only the 80s could imagine.

book497.title: Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children
book497.author: Ransom Riggs
book497.description: More than just peculiar, these children seem downright supernatural! Follow along this haunting adventure about found family and not fitting in, illustrated with vintage photography.

book498.title: Mont-Saint-Michel and Chartres
book498.author: Henry Adams
book498.description: A fictional travelogue, self-described as "not anything that can possibly be useful or instructive — but only a sense of what those centuries had to say, and a sympathy with their ways of saying it."

book499.title: Mother Night
book499.author: Kurt Vonnegut
book499.description: An American in Germany turned spy during World War II, is facing trial as a Nazi war criminal. Does the vital role he inadvertently played in the Nazi propaganda machine make him guilty?

book500.title: The Mousetrap and Other Plays
book500.author: Agatha Christie
book500.description: A locked room mystery in a snowbound bed and breakfast by The Queen of Crime. The Mousetrap opened at the Theatre Royal in Nottingham, England on October 6, 1952. The play met with such success it didn't leave the stage in 70 years, becoming history's longest running play.

book501.title: Mrs. Dalloway
book501.author: Virginia Woolf
book501.description: Get to know Clarissa as she prepares for a party later that evening. Learn about her life and meet her guests while pondering human nature and exploring the social structures of the 1920s. Will her party be a success?

book502.title: Much Ado About Nothing
book502.author: William Shakespeare
book502.description: A web of love, lies and misunderstandings encircle four lovers. Laugh along as their lives get turned upside down in this punny romp about jealousy and trust.

book503.title: Night and Day
book503.author: Virginia Woolf
book503.description: Can love and marriage coexist and is marriage necessary for happiness? Explore love and life in Edwardian London as night and day contrast just as the lives of Katherine and Mary.

book504.title: Night Sky with Exit Wounds
book504.author: Ocean Vuong
book504.description: This collection of poetry courageously explores violence and the delicacy of life. The author tells of the Vietnam War, of his experience with 9/11, and of queer love.

book505.title: On Beauty
book505.author: Zadie Smith
book505.description: Follow the increasingly intertwining lives of two very different academic families as their ideologies clash and their struggle with black identity and the nature of beauty unfolds.

book506.title: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous
book506.author: Ocean Vuong
book506.description: A novel written in the form of a letter, addressed from a son to his illiterate mother; a recipient who, like a ghost, is not promised - only longed for. Redolent of queer and feminist thinking, this is a raw and earnest exploration of race, class, and honesty.

book507.title: Orlando
book507.author: Virginia Woolf
book507.description: A medley through over three centuries of history, featuring a suave protagonist and lots of moments of self-discovery. Filled with passionate affairs, bittersweet moments, bending the rules of time, class, and gender.

book508.title: Othello
book508.author: William Shakespeare
book508.description: The heroic black general Othello soon finds himself in the middle of intrigue and betrayal after one fateful promotion. The start of a brutal tragedy about someone who “loved not wisely but too well”.

book509.title: P.S. I Still Love You
book509.author: Jenny Han
book509.description: In this bittersweet sequel to a YA bestseller, the turbulent romance continues. A gripping story with lots of twists and turns, beautiful moments, betrayals, and a charged game of Assassins.

book510.title: Pageboy
book510.author: Elliot Page
book510.description: This memoir details Page's journey of self-discovery, and of overcoming the many hurdles put up by a transphobic and misogynistic film industry, to get to where he is now.

book511.title: Parable of the Sower
book511.author: Octavia E. Butler
book511.description: In a dystopian world ravaged by climate change and corporate greed, a young woman embarks on a biblical journey to spread the seeds of a new religion in an attempt to redeem humanity.

book512.title: Persepolis; The Story of a Childhood
book512.author: Marjane Satrapi
book512.description: A visually stunning and bold graphic novel memoir following a young Iranian girl through the 1970s and 1980s. This gripping story explores themes of revolution, religion, family, history and daily life in the face of tumultuous times.

book513.title: Peter Pan in Kensington Gardens
book513.author: J. M. Barrie
book513.description: A story about a mischivious boy who becomes stuck "Betwixt-and-Between" childhood and growing up, between the real world and the magical world of Kensington Gardens after dark.

book515.title: Prince Caspian; The Return to Narnia
book515.author: C.S. Lewis
book515.description: In this second installment of the Chronicles of Narnia series our protagonists suddenly return to a changed Narnia, and must help their friends defeat an evil despot making a play for power.

book516.title: The Princess Bride
book516.author: William Goldman
book516.description: This fantasy story contains: battles of wit, feats of strength, rodents of unusual size, sword fights of revenge, and the truest of true love, all saturated with inconceivable levels of satire.

book517.title: Saga; Volume 9
book517.author: Brian K. Vaughan & Fiona Staples
book517.description: Star Wars meets Game of Thrones! This ninth entry in the Saga series of graphic novels explores fake news and genuine terror in an epic sci-fi setting. Prepare for a heart-warming tale full of tragic twists.

book518.title: Scott Pilgrim's Precious Little Life (#1)
book518.author: Bryan Lee O'Malley
book518.description: A quirky graphic novel about a nonchalant slacker turned romantic hero who must defeat his crush's seven evil exes. It's a pretty clever metaphor for feeling insecure about your new partners romantic past, or so I am told.

book519.title: Sense and Sensibility
book519.author: Jane Austen
book519.description: A tale of two sisters, romantic engagements, quarrels, and the difficulty of making sensible and sensual choices in matters of love and marriage of course. Austen's delightful wit and sharp characterizations are great as ever in this all-time classic.

book520.title: Sister Outsider
book520.author: Audre Lorde
book520.description: A collection of boundary-breaking essays and speeches in which author Audre Lorde negotiates her complex identity as a Black woman, lesbian, poet, activist, cancer survivor, mother, and feminist.

book521.title: Starstruck; (Deluxe Edition)
book521.author: Elaine Lee & Michael Kaluta
book521.description: It’s a tough galaxy out there, but somebody's gotta live in it, and it might as well be YOU! The brilliant, feminist, sci-fi play turned graphic novel that you may not have heard of yet.

book522.title: Stormbreaker
book522.author: Anthony Horowitz
book522.description: Ever dreamt of becoming a teenage spy for MI6 and uncovering a nefarious plot? The plot may be a little ridiculous but you probably won't care as you race along this thrilling first entry in the Alex Rider series.

book523.title: Sula
book523.author: Toni Morrison
book523.description: The story of the friendship between two young Black girls and the conflicting paths that their lives take them on. Read on as their opposing personalities affect the town in a tale about defying social norms, resentment and reconciliation.

book524.title: The Sunlit Man
book524.author: Brandon Sanderson
book524.description: Nomad has been jumping between different worlds to stay ahead of his pursuers. But with his diminished powers, he is trapped on a planet where the sun's intensity will kill, and finds himself caught up in a struggle between a despotic ruler and the defiant rebels.

book525.title: Supernova; Renegades #3
book525.author: Marissa Meyer
book525.description: The Renegades' greatest enemy is alive, a danger once more to Gatlon City. In this thrilling conclusion to the Renegades , Adrian and Nova struggle to protect those they love, all while keeping secrets from one another. When the dust settles, who will be left standing?

book526.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
book526.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
book526.description: Join the brilliant detective and his loyal companion on thrilling investigations as they unravel mysteries and outwit criminals in 12 legendary tales.

book527.title: The Book of Tea
book527.author: Okakura Kakuzo
book527.description: An open letter to the west, learn all about the Japanese values of Teaism and let them enrich your life. One of the great English tea classics that bridges the gap between the spritual and secular spheres of tea.

book528.title: The Book of the City of Ladies
book528.author: Christine de Pizan
book528.description: Guided by three allegorical figures, a woman builds a symbolic city with walls protecting women from slander and misogyny, celebrating their courage, wisdom, and achievements - radically ahead of its time in 15th-century Europe.

book529.title: Book of Yokai ; Mysterious Creatures of Japanese Folklore
book529.author: Michael Dylan Foster & Shinonome Kijin
book529.description: Yokai is a shorthand for all fantastical beings and supernatural phenomena in Japanese stories. This folkloric encyclopaedia is filled with their origins and meanings.

book530.title: The Canterbury Tales
book530.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
book530.description: Twenty-four stories told by twenty-four pilgrims as they travel to Canterbury Cathedral. Who can tell the most enthralling one and win a free meal at the Tabard Inn? This classic piece of English literature has been thought to have popularized the language in mainstream literature, but was it ever finished?

book531.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
book531.author: Alexandre Dumas
book531.description: In this epic tale of revenge, redemption, and exquisite French drama, a betrayed lover returns to the Parisian high society in search of sweet revenge.

book532.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
book532.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
book532.description: An unlikely band of heroes must go on a quest to destroy an evil ring once and for all. Their journey through Tolkien's vibrant fantasy world has become part of the foundation of modern fantasy literature.

book533.title: The Girl Who Played with Fire
book533.author: Stieg Larsson
book533.description: This book must be one of the darkest Nordic crime thrillers out there. Still, Larsson manages to sneak in moments of kindness and allyship that make this brutal revenge epos just barely possible to endure.

book534.title: The Green Ember; Book 1
book534.author: S.D. Smith & Zach Franzen
book534.description: Forced to flee their home, siblings Heather and Picket come to a hidden refuge where each rabbit trains their gifts to bring about a Mended Wood. Kids will love this series with its brave characters and themes of found family. Rabbits with swords!

book535.title: The Green Mile
book535.author: Stephen King
book535.description: The heart-wrenching story of a death-row inmate with magical abilities. Prepare for a sordid tale of a corrupt and cruel institution and of the mouse that survived it all.

book536.title: Greenglass House; Book 1
book536.author: Kate Milford & Jaime Zollars
book536.description: Milo has plans to exclusively munch on cookies and read books during his winter holidays. But thanks to a snow storm, his parents' inn fills with guests, all strangely invested in the story of their house. A locked room mystery and a treasure hunt, with a surprise twist!

book537.title: The Gunslinger
book537.author: Stephen King
book537.description: The last gunslinger's treacherous search for his ancient adversary leads him across an alternate reality Old West. A path full of monsters, demons and sacrifice lead to his ultimate destination: The Dark Tower.

book538.title: The House with a Clock in Its Walls
book538.author: John Bellairs
book538.description: A ticking time-clock threatens to destroy the world. A newbie and a local boy team up to stop the magical doomsday plot. Join them in this illustrated romp full of black magic, ghosts and derring-do.

book539.title: How Did Whales Get So Big?; An Other Curious Questions about Animals, Nature, Geology and Planet Earth
book539.author: MinuteEarth
book539.description: Are you a child who can't stop asking questions like, "Why did my hamster eat her babies?" Try this kid-friendly encyclopaedia! Filled with stick-figure illustrations and rigorous research., this STEM book is perfect for answering even the most curious kid's questions.

book540.title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
book540.author: C. S. Lewis
book540.description: In this delightful classic siblings stumble upon a magical world through an ordinary wardrobe, where talking animals and a wicked witch await.

book541.title: Listen for the Lie
book541.author: Amy Tintera
book541.description: Lucy doesn't want to be on a podcast about her best friend's murder. Her memory from that night is sketchy at best, and the town has already decided who's guilty. But true crime podcaster Ben is both persistent and attractive. Unputdownable and spicy!
